fields.description:
Summary

Operator_External_ID__c and Partner_External_ID__c are unique keys the CMS matches accounts on, and they are also embedded verbatim in every Deal External Deal ID — but nothing in Salesforce generates them. The current 63 values were typed into a spreadsheet during the initial import, so the format holds only by hand: one OP-FORTUNE WHEELZ would put a space into a key the CMS spec says is letters and digits, and it would surface as a rejected deal rather than a bad account.

This stamps both IDs in a before-save flow on Account, when the field is blank, from the same kind of derivation the Deal ID already uses. Operator = OP- + the account Name with punctuation and spaces removed, uppercased. Partner = PT- + Partner_Code__c, normalised the same way — Partner IDs are not name-derived, so the code remains the input, and the flow normalises that field too since it is hand-entered and also feeds the Deal key. If the derivation would produce an empty key, the save is blocked with a Custom Error rather than stamping a stub.

Fixing it at the source is what lets every downstream key trust these values, so the Account validation-rule guard originally drafted on BUILD-272 is cut rather than built.

Current state

  • Operator_External_ID__c and Partner_External_ID__c: both Text(80), unique, case-insensitive, external id. No automation writes either — populated entirely by the import.

  • Record type spread: 58 Operator, 5 Partner, 311 Player, 7 Referrer, 9 with no record type. Every Operator has an Operator ID; every Partner has a Partner ID; the other 327 accounts have neither and must not get one.

  • The derivation reproduces all 63 existing values exactly, verified record by record. Operators follow OP- + Name with spaces and punctuation stripped, uppercased — Fortune Wheelz to OP-FORTUNEWHEELZ, No Limit Coins to OP-NOLIMITCOINS, and Bally's to OP-BALLYS, which is the one case proving apostrophes are stripped too, not just spaces.

  • Partner IDs are not derivable from the name: Catena to PT-CTM, Cipher to PT-C, GDC to PT-GD, Dietz to PT-D, Direct to PT-DIRECT. These are the Airtable partner codes, so Partner_Code__c is the only valid input.

  • Partner_Code__c is Text(40), not unique, hand-entered, and its description still frames it as a reporting convenience — it is now part of two CMS-facing keys.

  • Account.Name is already required for business accounts, so a truly blank Operator name is unreachable on every path. What is reachable is a name that normalises to empty — whitespace-only, or punctuation-only like --- — which would derive the stub OP-. That, not blankness, is the case the guard has to catch.

  • A blank Partner_Code__c is fully reachable — the field is optional, so a Partner can be created without one via UI, API or data loader.

Proposed solution

1. New flow Account_Before_Save_Set_External_Ids — before-save, create and update, no entry filter on the ID fields (the blank check is a Decision, matching the Deal pattern so a manual clear regenerates).

Gate on record type by RecordType.DeveloperName, never a hardcoded RecordTypeId — Ids differ between sandbox and production and would break the deployment.

Element order: Start → Decision Record_Type? → Operator branch / Partner branch / (neither) End.

2. Operator branch — when RecordType.DeveloperName = 'Operator':

  • Leave Name itself alone (it is the user's to control).

  • Guard: if LEN({!fxCleanName}) = 0 → Custom Error targeted at the Name field: "Operator name must contain at least one letter or number — it is used to generate the Operator External ID that the WagerTech CMS matches this account on."

  • When ISBLANK({!$Record.Operator_External_ID__c}) → assign {!fxOperatorExtId}:

"OP-" & UPPER(
SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(
SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(
TRIM({!$Record.Name}),
" ", ""), "'", ""), "’", ""), "-", ""), ".", ""),
",", ""), "&", ""), "/", ""), "(", ""), ")", "")
)

Salesforce formulas have no regex replace, so the strip is an explicit SUBSTITUTE chain. The curly apostrophe is in the list deliberately — it arrives via copy-paste and is invisible in a page layout.

3. Partner branch — when RecordType.DeveloperName = 'Partner':

  • Always assign Partner_Code__c = {!fxCleanCode} (the same chain applied to Partner_Code__c instead of Name). Normalising rather than blocking keeps data loads and updates unblocked, and the field is a code, so uppercasing it silently is safe.

  • Guard: if LEN({!fxCleanCode}) = 0 → Custom Error targeted at the Partner_Code__c field: "Partner Code is required and must contain at least one letter or number — it generates the Partner External ID and is built into every Deal ID sent to the WagerTech CMS."

  • When ISBLANK({!$Record.Partner_External_ID__c}) → assign "PT-" & {!fxCleanCode}.

3a. Why the guard lives in the flow and not in a validation rule

The guard is not a failsafe — the flow needs it to be correct. Without it a blank code stamps the stub PT-, which the unique index then owns, so the next blank-code Partner fails with a raw DUPLICATE_VALUE pointing at a record that has nothing to do with it. One malformed save poisons every later one.

That inverts the usual ordering: the flow is the primary control and a validation rule would be the redundant copy. Before-save flows run before validation rules, both cover every path (UI, API, data loader, Apex), and a Custom Error can target a specific field so it renders inline exactly like a validation rule would. Building both means the same rule in two places that can drift. Decided: flow only, no validation rule.

3b. Make Partner Code mandatory in the UI — part of this ticket

The flow is the hard control; this is the prompt that keeps users from meeting it. Follow the BUILD-249 pattern rather than field-level required:

  • Mark the Partner_Code__c component required in Dynamic Forms on the Partner record page. Not field-level required, no validation rule — UI creation demands it while API, flow and data-load paths stay open (the flow guard covers those).

  • Verify the New Partner path honours it. If that modal still renders the classic layout, mark the field required there too.

  • Place it near Partner Name / Partner Type, not buried in a later section.

Raise with WagerTech before or alongside the build. Partner Code is NOT in Emily's mandatory-field list on BUILD-269 (Name, Logo, Partner Portal, Primary Contact) — this is a Jumpr addition driven by the External ID depending on it. Tell her that, rather than letting a rep discover a new required field. There are only 5 Partners and all already have codes, so nothing existing is blocked.

Convention note: layout-required is a deliberate exception to the Aug 17 rule that nothing is marked required on layouts — the same exception already granted for Source on Deal (BUILD-249), and for the same reason: a validation rule would also block updates to legacy records.

4. Duplicate handling — loud, no counter. Both ID fields are already unique, so two accounts normalising to the same value fail on the index. Add a Custom Error naming the existing account so the message is actionable:

"An account with this External ID already exists: {existing account Name}. External IDs are generated from the account name (Operator) or Partner Code (Partner), so two records cannot share one. Check whether this account is a duplicate, or adjust the name/code."

No -002 counter, deliberately: the CMS maps accounts by external id, so a counter-suffixed account would be a second identity for the same real-world operator.

5. Partner_Code__c description — replace the current text:

Field Description (paste as-is): Short uppercase code identifying this partner (e.g. CTM for Catena, GD for GDC). Set by the user, then normalised on save by flow Account - Before Save - Set External Ids: spaces and punctuation removed, forced uppercase. This value is embedded in Partner_External_ID__c AND in every Deal External Deal ID sent to the WagerTech CMS, so changing it on an existing partner does not retro-update those keys — treat it as fixed once deals exist against the partner.

Help Text (paste as-is): Short uppercase code for this partner, letters and digits only (e.g. CTM, GD). Used in the Partner External ID and in Deal IDs sent to the CMS — set it once and leave it.

6. No backfill. All 63 existing IDs already match what the flow would generate, so there is nothing to correct. Verify by spot-checking rather than by rewriting: no existing ID should change value when its account is re-saved. All 5 Partners already have codes, so the new guard blocks nothing that exists today.

Acceptance criteria

  1. A new Operator saved with a blank ID gets OP- + its uppercased, stripped name. Verify with a multi-word name and one containing an apostrophe.

  2. A new Partner with a Partner Code gets PT- + the cleaned code.

  3. Partner Code is normalised on every save — {{ctm }} becomes CTM — while the Partner External ID stays frozen.

  4. Empty derivations are blocked, not stamped. A Partner saved with a blank or punctuation-only Partner Code is blocked with the error on that field; an Operator whose name normalises to nothing is blocked with the error on Name. In neither case is a stub PT- or OP- written.

  5. The blank-code block holds on every path — UI, API and data loader — and no PT- value exists in the org afterwards to poison later saves.

  6. Existing IDs never change. Re-saving all 58 Operators and 5 Partners, including after a rename, leaves every Operator_External_ID__c and Partner_External_ID__c byte-identical.

  7. Clearing an ID and saving regenerates it from the current name or code.

  8. Player, Referrer and no-record-type accounts are untouched — no ID stamped, no Partner Code written.

  9. A second account normalising to an existing ID is blocked with the Custom Error naming the existing account; no -002 value is ever produced.

  10. The flow references RecordType.DeveloperName, not a hardcoded RecordTypeId, and deploys to a second org without edits.

  11. Partner Code is required in the UI — a new Partner cannot be saved from the record page or the New modal without it, while API, flow and data-load paths remain open.

  12. No validation rule is created on Account.

Out of scope

  • Retro-updating IDs after a rename, and any drift flag for it — the CMS matches accounts on the stored ID and does not re-derive it, so a rename is harmless.

  • Getting WagerTech to map a newly created account on the CMS side; until they do, deals on it are rejected as unknown_operator / unknown_partner. Operational, not a build step.

  • Making Partner_Code__c unique — worth considering separately, but it would need a duplicate cleanup first.

  • Partner-name duplicate rules — those stay in BUILD-08.

Output

One flow deployed in Partial SB, metadata retrieved and committed; Partner_Code__c description, help text and Dynamic-Forms-required setting applied; the Partner Code requirement raised with WagerTech; spot-check results recorded on this ticket.

Deal\__c already has the logic a \`region\` field needs — it's just embedded separately inside the Deal Name and External Deal ID before-save flows instead of living on a reusable field. Add a new formula field, Region_Codec, that surfaces that value directly, matching the CMS webhook's own region format: US state deals get a US- prefix (US-NJ), Canadian province deals don't (AB), and country-wide deals resolve to US/CA. Reuses Market_State_Code_\_c's existing state CASE logic rather than adding a third copy of the 64-value list.

**Proposed solution**

1\. Add formula field Region_Code\__c (Text) on Deal_\_c:

IF(

ISPICKVAL(Market_State__c, ""),

CASE(TEXT(Market_Country__c),

"United States", "US",

"Canada", "CA",

""),

IF(

TEXT(Market_Country__c) = "United States",

"US-" & Market_State_Code__c,

Market_State_Code__c

)

)

2\. No page layout placement — automation/reporting field only, same pattern as Market_State_Code\__c, Market_Country_Codec, Source_Code_\_c (BUILD-246).

Field Description (ready to paste):

fields.description:
## Summary

The Deal before-save flow appends `-002`, `-003` … to `External_Deal_ID__c` when a base key already exists. Once BUILD-272 ships, that path is unreachable: a second Deal on the same makeup is rejected at the Custom Error, and would die on the unique index anyway. The counter is left standing there deliberately, because removing it presumes an answer to a question that is still open — how a deal whose commercial terms changed is represented.

This card holds that scope. It is deliberately unsized and has no acceptance criteria yet; both follow from the 2026-09-11 sync and from DECISION-07.

## Current state

* `Get_Highest_Match` (SOQL on `External_Deal_ID__c` by base-key prefix) → `fxNextSuffix` → `fxFinalId`, with `Set_External_Id` assigning `fxFinalId`. Untouched by BUILD-272.
* Never fired on a surviving record: all 28 Deals were checked on 2026-09-08 and every counter-shaped id is a hand-seeded load value. The deleted 2026-09-01 ReBet duplicate is the one likely case it did fire.
* After BUILD-272 the counter costs one SOQL query per Deal save and returns nothing. It is also untestable, which means a future reader will reasonably assume versioning works when it does not.

## The three directions, and what each one costs

**A — Delete the counter.** `Set_External_Id` assigns `fxBaseKey` directly; `Get_Highest_Match`, `fxNextSuffix` and `fxFinalId` are removed. One flow version, drops a query from every save. This is the only direction that needs nothing from WagerTech, and it is the original BUILD-272 step 2.

**B — Replace it with a manual version or suffix selector.** A user-set field feeds the id instead of an automatic counter. This only changes anything if the version also becomes part of `Deal_Makeup_Key__c` — otherwise the duplicate block still rejects the second deal before the selector is ever read. And the moment it does become part of the key, the Salesforce unique constraint stops mirroring the CMS rule, so Salesforce will save a pair the CMS rejects with `makeup_owned_by_other`. Needs a CMS answer first.

**C — Keep versioning and relax the dedupe: allow a repeat makeup when every prior deal carrying it is retired or closed.** The dedupe lookup gains a status filter and the unique index has to be reconsidered, because a unique index cannot be conditional. Depends entirely on whether the CMS releases the combination when a deal goes inactive — the current working assumption is that it does not, and that assumption is written into `Deal_Makeup_Key__c`'s field description and BUILD-272's AC 4. If it lands here, both are edits.

## What has to be true before this can be scoped

1. **Does the CMS release the makeup combination when a deal is retired, closed or made inactive?** WagerTech to confirm — this is DECISION-07 question 3, and B and C both collapse without it.
2. Does anyone need to see a deal's terms as at a past date, or is the current value enough? (DECISION-07 question 1 — decides whether versioning is a real requirement or an artefact of the id format.)
3. If versioning survives in any form, is the version visible to reps, or an internal id detail only?

## Dependencies

* **DECISION-07** — carries the decision; this card carries the build. Do not restate the options here once that card is updated.
* **BUILD-272** — must ship first. This card only ever edits a flow version that BUILD-272 creates.
* **BUILD-273** — the cleanup/regeneration pass. If direction A or B changes the id format, regeneration has to run after this card, not before, or it runs twice.

## Output

To be defined after the 2026-09-11 sync.

_Confirm with WagerTech (Emily/Lina) which Deal fields must be snapshotted onto a Sign-Up at completion, and which Deal fields can change over a Deal's lifecycle and need dated history. Feeds directly into DECISION-07 and the Commercial Terms history object design._

## Why this matters

* Sign-Up payout reporting must reflect the commercial terms in effect when the Sign-Up completed, not the Deal's current values

* Not yet a fixed field list — needs WagerTech confirmation

* Design for the Deal / Commercial Terms history object is blocked on this list

* Flagged as the priority blocker for that design work

## What needs confirming with WagerTech

* Which Deal fields must be captured as a snapshot on the Sign-Up record at completion
* Which Deal fields can change during a Deal's lifecycle and need dated history (versioned Deal vs. related Commercial Terms object)
* Whether backdating a changed term needs to recompute already-completed Sign-Ups

* A real example already occurred: a CPA change was backdated 10 days into the month

## Field list to validate (updated from live Deal page, 2026-09-11)

* Payout Model — how commission is calculated (e.g. CPA vs. Rev Share)

* Commercial Terms section

* Currency

* Commercial Terms section — currency changes are handled as a new Deal, not tracked on this one

* Monthly Cap

* Commercial Terms section

* Deposit Range Min / Deposit Range Max / Deposit Range

* Commercial Terms section — three separate fields on the page, unclear if Deposit Range duplicates Min/Max or is distinct

* Avg Deposit Target

* Commercial Terms section

* Qualifying Action

* Commercial Terms section

* Redeposit Required

* Redeposit Details section

* Effective Start Date / Effective End Date

* Additional Details section

* CPA Amount

## Open gap — CPA

* CPA / commission rate is not a visible field anywhere in the Commercial Terms section on the live Deal page (confirmed via screenshot of ON-HARDROCK-C-CASINO-WT, 2026-09-11)

* Need to confirm with WagerTech whether it lives on the Admin tab, is derived from Payout Model, or is tracked at the Deal Rep Assignment level instead
* This must be resolved before the field list goes final — CPA is the term referenced most in the commercial-terms discussion

## Notes

* Blocks DECISION-07 and the Commercial Terms history object design.

fields.description:
Verify the one dependency we cannot check from outside before committing to the \~56h build.

Breakdown:

* Salesforce authentication plumbing, reused as-is by the build — 4h

* Direct-to-Drive upload probe, including whether Google permits browser-to-Google uploads from a Salesforce page (§4.2) — 5h

* Minimal test component and screen-flow embed check — 2h

* Test at realistic file sizes, document findings, recommend a path — 1h

EXIT CRITERIA

* GO: authentication reliable, upload and viewing work, an interrupted upload leaves no orphaned file behind, no blocking org policy, one path demonstrably sound. Proceed to build reusing the POC's auth work

* CONDITIONAL GO: works with a constraint worth weighing (e.g. a file-size ceiling). Report the constraint and its cost; WagerTech decides

* NO-GO: something blocks it, e.g. an org policy we cannot work around. Stop and report before further effort

Recommended architecture is Option B (browser sends direct to Drive) — removes a whole category of chunking code rather than adding it, and does not need revisiting if file sizes grow. Option A (Salesforce relays) is a known-good fallback since the existing Dropbox integration proves it works at current file sizes; would be sized from POC findings, not guessed now.

Blocked on WagerTech prerequisites C1-C7 (BUILD-94).

Source: Drive Storage doc §4.3, §6.

BILLING: SOW assumes native Salesforce storage, so this comes through as a change order. Client sign-off on the doc authorises the POC ONLY; the build is authorised separately after findings.
fields.summary: BUILD-93 — Google Drive proof storage: Proof of Concept (12h)

comments.body:
**APPROVED TO PROCEED — 2026-08-04. Client explicitly reprioritised this ahead of the CMS API work.**

Kobi had proposed tabling it \[47:22\]: "if this is not urgent, I would table this for later, and focus on deal and deal rep assignment and CMS API work first."

Joyce reversed that \[48:11\]: "if you were waiting on us for like the deal stuff and the GCP integration seems pretty straightforward, like folder structure aside, I would probably focus your efforts on the GCP while we're like 100% confirming stuff… internally on the deal side of things."

Emily signed off on the design \[52:00\]: "I think like what we've been talking around here, Kobi, then I think you're good."

**Not blocked on folder structure.** Agreed the POC proves file transfer and API calls first; folder hierarchy is iterative.

**Confirmed scope boundaries:**

* Target is **Google Drive via a service account**, not GCP proper. Kobi \[53:00\]: "what we're proposing here, it's Google Drive, essentially, through a service account where we're storing everything. Very similar to Dropbox."

* **No compression, no encryption** in scope — service-account security only.

* Files tagged by proof type on upload (sign-up / deposit / wager).

* Sign Up records keep the **link-paste** proof fields for Phase 1. Button-upload is the POC, not the Phase 1 UX.

**#1 requirement — per-rep walled garden.** Joyce \[43:14\]: "you should only have access and visibility over your own proofs… it's like a walled garden per rep", plus "a separate provision for like operations role to be able to see everything." Proposed hierarchy (not final): rep → player name → operator / sign up → date.

**Client-side dependencies:** service account provisioning is "an Alex thing" (Emily \[52:52\]). Emily also asked whether the required Drive permission scope is documented in the design doc — Kobi owes that: "It should. If not, I'll get that for you." \[54:14\]

fields.description:
Client-owed inputs, tracked so an unassigned owner does not silently become the schedule.

\[POC\] needed to start:

* C1 Google Cloud project with the Drive API enabled — nothing can begin without this

* C2 A service account created in that project — the identity Salesforce authenticates as

* C3 Confirmation the Google org policy PERMITS SERVICE-ACCOUNT KEYS. Many enterprise tenants block these by default. Alternatives exist but add effort — we would come back with options rather than proceed

* C4 The service-account credential made available to us. 1Password shared vault is our usual route; equally happy to have their admin paste it straight into Salesforce on a screenshare. NEVER over email or chat

* C5 A NAMED Google Workspace admin who can action C1-C7, plus a target date. The single biggest schedule risk on this work is an unassigned owner, not the build

* C6 A test SHARED DRIVE the service account can write to — must be a Shared Drive, NOT a folder in someone's personal Drive. A service account has no usable storage allowance of its own so uploads to a personal Drive fail on quota

* C7 Confirmation of maximum file size and accepted file types. Working assumption is short phone recordings, 10-20s, a few MB to \~50MB

\[Build\] needed only on a go decision:

* C8 A permanent Shared Drive for production proofs, service account as Content Manager, their admins as Managers, reps added as members. Rep membership is what gives reps the ability to open proof links

Source: Drive Storage doc §5, §11.

fields.description:
Build the file container once, generically, instead of adding proof-specific fields.

Why: three proof URL fields on Sign-Up means EXACTLY THREE FILES, FOREVER. It cannot hold a second attempt at a proof, and it cannot hold anything that is not one of those three things. Payouts and deposits are obvious next candidates.

* Cloud_File__c — one record per uploaded file regardless of what it relates to. Fields: Category (Welcome/Deposit/Wager Proof, Other, extensible), Drive file ID (permanent path-independent handle), File link, File name/size/type, Uploaded by, Uploaded at, Status (Active/Superseded so a replaced proof keeps its history), Storage provider (Google Drive/Dropbox so both coexist during transition), Sign-Up

* RECORD TYPES FROM THE START — 'Sign-Up File' now. Retrofitting record types onto an object with live records means reclassifying every one of them: \~1h of config now vs a data cleanup exercise later

* Three lookups on Sign-Up point at the current Welcome, Deposit and Wager proof so the page still shows 'here is the deposit proof' at a glance; replaced proofs and everything else appear in a related list below

* THE EXISTING PROOF URL FIELDS STAY and are populated automatically on upload. The URL field is the fast path for viewing (one click), the file record is the system of record. This is why current screens, proof indicators and Completion % keep working untouched, and why Dropbox and Drive links coexist with nothing downstream needing to know the difference

* Two consequences of a generic container, both priced in: each file record carries its own visibility setting rather than inheriting the parent's (D6), and deleting a parent does not remove its files — needs cleanup of orphans

Adding the next parent later (payouts, deposits, deals) is a new record type, a relationship field and a related list — \~1-2h each, not a redesign.

Effort: 8h. Dropping this saves 8h but caps WagerTech at three files per sign-up permanently.

Source: Drive Storage doc §2.1, D2.

As a Brand Manager or Ops user, I want to see whether a deal reached the CMS and force a re-send when it did not.

* CMS_Sync_Status__c picklist (Not Published / Pending / Synced / Failed / Retrying)

* CMS_Sync_Note__c Long Text Area (2000) — most recent attempt's message

* CMS_Last_Sync_Attempt\__c, CMS_Last_Sync_Success_\_c DateTime — lets Ops distinguish 'synced' from 'synced, but six days ago'

* All grouped in the Ops section of the Deal record page

* Field History Tracking enabled on CMS_Sync_Status__c so the pattern of failures over time is visible

* The 'Sync with CMS' button calls the SAME invocable Apex as the automatic path — no duplicate code path

* Button visible to Brand Manager and Ops only via dynamic action visibility; NEVER visible to reps

* Repeated presses are safe; the CMS receives a normal update event

* Automatic retry: three attempts with backoff before status is set to Failed

* On failure the note contains HTTP status and response body, truncated to field length

* Sync fields exist on Deal ONLY, not on Deal Link — publish is deal-scoped, links inherit their deal's sync state

* List-view mass action supports bulk retry after a CMS outage

Effort: 8-12h. Blocked by BUILD-66.

Source: CMS Integration Design v1, §4.4.

* Link_Code_Snapshot__c is populated at write time and survives a later rename or deletion of the link record

* Active-period behaviour verified end to end per D13: status entering Active sets Effective From, leaving Active sets Effective To, both captured in history so the full sequence of periods is reconstructable

* History remains read-only to all profiles, including the integration user

As the CMS, I need to write assignments against a stable key I own and have Salesforce resolve the rep, so sync is idempotent and every Salesforce record traces back to its CMS record.

* Deal_Rep_Assignment\__c.DRA_External_Id_\_c — Text(255), External Id, Unique, NOT required (migrated records will not have one)

* Upsert on that key creates or updates correctly; replaying an identical call is a no-op beyond field updates

* Rep resolution follows external Id -> slug -> email, first match wins, and relates the user to the assignment

* Zero or multiple matches set Assignment_Status__c = Review Required with a note recording what was attempted

* The integration user's permission set covers the new field

Effort: 3-5h. Assumes the rep identifier fields on the User record are in place from the sign-up logging build.

Source: CMS Integration Design v1, §5.1 + Appendix A.

NOTE: Appendix A lists this as blocked by D9, but §1.2 commits Jumpr to building it in parallel ahead of Direction 1 so the CMS team has a working sandbox endpoint. Treating as Up Next — D9 only governs the fallback identity approach, not the field itself.

* Report 'Deals — Published but Never Synced': published with no successful sync recorded — catches deals that never achieved a first successful push

* Optional: scheduled alert for deals sitting in Failed beyond a defined threshold (+\~2h)

Effort: 2-3h. Blocked by BUILD-83.

Source: CMS Integration Design v1, §4.4.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: covers Salesforce-side errors only — failures of the callout itself up to a non-success HTTP response. Once the CMS acknowledges a payload, Salesforce marks the deal Synced and has no further visibility. Anything the CMS does after acknowledging needs CMS-side monitoring. Same in reverse: Salesforce cannot report on Direction 2 calls that never arrive.

comments.body:
Hi [@Kobi Kunasekaran](https://app.asana.com/1/1202721605677544/profile/1203115293332591), see below the things we can build ahead of the CMS sandbox. 

* **Auth & connection design**: External Credential (Custom auth, one principal, header `X-Webhook-Key`) → Named Credential at `https://wagertech-cms-tkqruf7sva-uk.a.run.app`, callout path `callout:<NamedCredential>/api/salesforce/deals`. Only the click-through setup and dropping the real secret into the principal wait on access.
* **Field mapping**: All core payload fields already exist — `External_Deal_ID__c`, `Operator_External_ID__c`, `Partner_External_ID__c`, `Vertical__c`, `Source__c`, `Deal_Status__c`, `CurrencyIsoCode`, `Effective_Start_Date__c`. No new fields needed for the payload itself.
* **Region derivation**: `region` isn't a stored field — needs logic derived from `Market_Country__c` + `Market_State__c`. Can be spec'd now.
* **New fields to design**: `Sync_Status__c` (picklist), a sync-error detail field, `Last_Synced_Date__c`, optionally a self-lookup `Superseded_By__c` for Retire & Replace.
* **Flow design**: record-triggered Flow on Deal__c (trigger conditions, HTTP Callout, fault path), a validation rule locking the five makeup fields once Active, and a uniqueness check across the makeup combination - if not yet existing.
* **Error handling & retry design**: retryable-vs-terminal split is already given (503/timeouts retry; 400/401/409/422 need a fix first). Can spec a `CMS_Sync_Log__c` audit object and an Apex Queueable for bulk resync (≤200/call).
* **Permissions**: field-level security plan for the new sync fields. 

Most of the big questions are already covered, but I have a quick question about retries:

* **Retry strategy — automated vs. manual?** The doc splits failures into two classes: 503/timeout/network (explicitly safe and welcome to retry) vs. 400/401/409/422 (explicitly "do not loop... need a fix first"). Given that split, do we: 

* Build automated background retry (capped attempts + backoff) for transient failures only, and leave business-rule failures (400/409/422) as surface-and-fix-manually?
* Or keep everything manual for V1 — surface all failures the same way and require a person to trigger every resend, transient or not?
* Separately: for `unknown_operator`/`unknown_partner` rejections, the fix happens on WagerTech's side (they map the account in the CMS), not in Salesforce — so nothing on the Deal record changes to naturally re-trigger a resend. Do we need a manual "Resend to CMS" action just for that case?
* And do we want an admin-triggered bulk resync (the Apex Queueable already specced for up to 200/call) as a safety net for "CMS was down and a batch of deals are stuck," independent of whichever retry approach we pick?

fields.description:
Mirrors BUILD-265, built for Operator instead of Partner. Header roll-up counts of distinct Partners and distinct Sources across an Operator's related Deals.

## Fields

* Associated_Partners_List__c — Text(255), hidden from every layout. Stores the raw DLRS output.
* Associated_Partners\__c — Number, Formula. Reads Associated_Partners_List_\_c. This is the field users see.
* Operator_Associated_Sources_List__c — Text(255), hidden from every layout. Stores the raw DLRS output.
* Operator_Associated_Sources\__c — Number, Formula. Reads Operator_Associated_Sources_List_\_c. This is the field users see.

## Why the Sources field names differ from Partner

Operator and Partner are both record types on the same Account object. Partner already uses Associated_Sources\__c and Associated_Sources_Listc, built in BUILD-265. Those exact names cannot be reused here — they already exist on the object. Use the Operator_ prefixed names above instead.

## Implementation Requirements

* Create both helper fields as Text, length 255. Do not use Long Text Area — Salesforce blocks LEN and SUBSTITUTE from referencing a Long Text Area field inside a Formula field. This surfaced during the BUILD-265 build and cost real time; skip it here.
* Create both count fields with Data Type set to Formula, not Text and not Number directly. On the next screen, set Formula Return Type to Number, 0 decimal places. Picking Text by mistake here produces a one-time Default Value instead of a live formula — also hit during BUILD-265.
* Formula for Associated_Partners\__c: IF(ISBLANK(Associated_Partners_Listc), 0, LEN(Associated_Partners_Listc) - LEN(SUBSTITUTE(Associated_Partners_List_\_c, ";", "")) + 1)
* Formula for Operator_Associated_Sources\__c: IF(ISBLANK(Operator_Associated_Sources_Listc), 0, LEN(Operator_Associated_Sources_Listc) - LEN(SUBSTITUTE(Operator_Associated_Sources_List_\_c, ";", "")) + 1)
* Build two DLRS records. Parent Object: Account. Child Object: Deal\__c. Relationship Field on both: Operator_\_c (confirmed API name from the BUILD-265 build).
* Associated Partners rollup: Field to Aggregate = Partner\__c (confirmed API name). Aggregate Operation = Concatenate Distinct. Aggregate Result Field = Associated_Partners_List_\_c.
* Associated Sources rollup: Field to Aggregate = Source\__c. Aggregate Operation = Concatenate Distinct. Aggregate Result Field = Operator_Associated_Sources_List_\_c.
* Set Concatenate Delimiter to a semicolon on both DLRS records, matching the formulas exactly.
* Set Calculation Mode to Realtime and Calculation Sharing Mode to User on both, matching the Partner build.
* Run Full Calculate on both DLRS records after saving. Realtime mode only fires on new Deal saves going forward — it will not backfill existing Deals on its own.
* Add both formula count fields, not the helper fields, to the Highlights Panel on the Operator Lightning page. Confirm the page uses Dynamic Highlights Panel, not the classic Highlights Panel, before adding — click the panel header in App Builder to check.

## Open Questions

* Deal scope: does the count include every related Deal, or Active-status only? Same open question as BUILD-265, still unresolved there.
* Blank Source__c on a Deal: counted as one distinct value, or excluded? Same open question as BUILD-265, still unresolved there.
* Whatever answer resolves these on BUILD-265 should be applied here too, for consistency between the two objects.

## Source

Emily Vandenberg, Wagertech feedback — Operator & Partner Record Pages doc, WAGERTECH Feedback OPERATOR section: "Add roll-up fields to header: # of associated partners and sources"

fields.description:
## Summary

When an Active Player has no completed sign-ups (or other qualifying activity) in the last 90 days, set their Status to Inactive.

## Context

Without an aging rule, players stay Active forever and reporting overstates the active base. The client set the threshold at **90 days without qualifying activity**. Qualifying activity is measured by Account.Last_Activity_Date__c.

## Current state

No scheduled automation exists on Account. Player_Status_Reason\__c already includes the value Inactivity. Field history tracking on Player_Statusc is off. In Partial today no Player is Active and no Last_Activity_Date_\_c is set, so first activation is safe by definition.

## Proposed solution

1. NEW schedule-triggered flow Player_Scheduled_Set_Inactive, daily 02:00 ET, on Account. Selects Players (Player record type) that are **Active** with a Last Activity Date **more than 90 days in the past**. Players at Pending, Banned, or Inactive, or with a blank Last Activity Date, are never touched. How eligibility is filtered (entry criteria vs. in-flow decision) is the developer's call — the boundary behavior is defined in the acceptance criteria.
2. Per eligible record: set Inactive and Player_Status_Reason__c = Inactivity. (Audit stamping via BUILD-251; the stamped updater will read "Automated Process" — expected.)
3. The 90-day threshold must be defined in **exactly one place** in the flow, named and documented so it's easy to find and change. Upgrade to a custom setting only if the client asks to tune it.
4. Enable field history tracking on Player_Status__c (audit trail for all status changes).

Testing note: feel free to adjust the inactivity threshold to 2–3 days or shorter to confirm the scheduled flow runs as expected, or manually set the Completed Dates/Activity Dates to simulate older completions.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An Active Player 91+ days stale flips to Inactive with Reason = Inactivity on the next run; exactly 90 days stays Active (boundary).
2. Must NOT evaluate: blank Last_Activity_Date__c, Pending, Banned, or players reactivated since their last activity.
3. A reactivated player is only re-flipped after a fresh 90-day lapse.
4. Bulk-safe at 200+ eligible records.

## Output

Scheduled flow deployed + activated in Partial SB; history tracking enabled; API names + first-run record count recorded on this ticket; requirements doc updated.

| Account | CustomObject | Update Component | Enable Account Field History |

| Account.Player_Status__c | CustomField | Update Component | Enable Field History |

**Testing:** Validated in sandbox via flow debug. To simulate the 90-day inactivity scenario within the test data's timeframe, the inactivity threshold on Account_Scheduled_Player_Set_Inactive was temporarily changed to 1 day. Debug run confirms Active Players with a Last Activity Date older than the threshold correctly flip to Inactive with Player_Status_Reason__c = Inactivity. Threshold to be reverted to 90 days before this is considered final.

**Scenario 2:** Activated the scheduled flow with `InactivityThresholdDays` set to 2 days.

Header stats derived from related Deals. Use DLRS. Deal to Operator and Deal to Partner are lookup relationships, not master-detail. Native rollup summary fields do not work on lookups.

## FIELDS

* On Partner: Associated Operators (distinct count of Operator across related Deals) / Associated Sources (distinct count of Source__c across related Deals)

## IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

* Use DLRS. Do not use the native rollup summary field type.

* Use DLRS CONCATENATE to build the distinct value list. Count the distinct values in a formula field. This matches the pattern already used for Supported Verticals and Supported Markets.

* Use Flow as the fallback method only if DLRS hits a limit.

* Use the correct child relationship on Deal for each rollup. BUILD-132 renamed these to Deals Partner and Deals Operator. Operator rollups read from Deals Operator. Partner rollups read from Deals Partner. A mix-up here causes a silent failure.

* Place both new fields in the Dynamic Highlights Panel on each record page. Do not use the compact layout. Both Operator and Partner already use Dynamic Lightning record pages built with Dynamic Forms (BUILD-135). The Dynamic Highlights Panel accepts any field, including a roll-up field, without adding it elsewhere on the page.

* Set both fields to read-only. No user gets edit access.

## OPEN QUESTIONS

* Scope the Deal population for each count. Decide if the count includes every related Deal, or only Deals with Deal Status = Active. The existing Active Deals rollup on both objects counts Active status only.

* Decide the behavior when Source__c is blank on a Deal. Confirm if a blank Source counts as one distinct value or gets excluded from the count.

## NOTES

* The same ask appears on both the Operator and Partner feedback lists: "# of associated partners and sources" (Operator) and "# of associated operators and sources" (Partner). Combined into one ticket, following the same convention as BUILD-132 (OP-9 + PT-10) and BUILD-148 (Operator + Partner rollups).

## Summary

External_Deal_ID\__c is the key the CMS configures against, and two same-shape deals differing only by source currently collide into an opaque -002 counter instead of carrying the source that distinguishes them. \*Solution: the External Deal ID flow includes -{Source_Code_\_c} inside the base key, before the uniqueness counter — e.g. BETMGM-DIRECT-ON-CAS-S; duplicate → BETMGM-DIRECT-ON-CAS-S-002.\* Extends BUILD-228.

## Current state

Flow `Deal_Before_Save_Set_External_Deal_ID` builds fxBaseKey = {TEST-}{Operator External ID minus "OP-"}~~{Partner_Code__c}~~{geo}-{vertical abbr}, queries Get_Highest_Match for existing IDs starting with the base key, and appends -002/-003… via fxNextSuffix (overflow guard at 999). Entry filter: runs only when External_Deal_ID__c is null → existing IDs are never rewritten (this enforces the no-retroactive-change decision).

## Proposed solution

1. Append -{Source_Code__c} (when non-blank, from BUILD-246) to fxBaseKey. **Must be part of fxBaseKey, before the uniqueness counter** — if appended after the counter, fxNextSuffix's RIGHT/LEN parsing breaks.
2. Verify counter behavior with a duplicate-insert test in sandbox: fxNextSuffix derives the counter by stripping LEN(fxBaseKey), so including Source in the base key is safe by construction — confirm it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Existing before-save trigger; no new trigger.
2. Two deals identical except Source (S vs V) get distinct base keys with no counter; true duplicates (same Source) still get -002.
3. Source blank → ID format unchanged from today.
4. Existing Deals keep their current External Deal ID — the null-only entry filter must remain in place.
5. External Deal ID remains unique across the org.

## Out of scope

* SLC-side matching changes (CMS already sends Deal_External_Id__c verbatim).
* Deal Number (DL-####) — Source does not join it (Kobi decision 2026-08-31).

fields.summary: Sign-Up — Stamp First Click Date and reactivate Inactive Deal from qualifying activity

fields.description:
## Summary

When a Sign-Up is completed: a **Pending or Inactive** Player becomes Active, and the Player's first/last completed sign-up dates (and Last Activity Date) are stamped. **Banned and already-Active Players never have their status changed** by this automation.

## Context

Players start at Player_Status__c = Pending when the SLC intake flows create them. The player's **first completed Sign-Up** should automatically move them to Active, and any completed Sign-Up should reactivate an Inactive player. (Today Inactive only ever means inactivity — see the epic's out-of-scope note on future reason-based gating.) Ops also wants first/last completed sign-up dates on the Player for reporting. This story is the single automation for "a Sign-Up just completed → update the Player."

## Current state

Account.First_Completed_Sign_Up\__c (Lookup → Sign_Up_\_c) exists, unpopulated — the stamping logic was drafted in a BUILD-177 comment but never implemented. No first/last-completed date fields exist on Account. Audit stamping is handled centrally by BUILD-251 (prerequisite).

## Proposed solution

1. NEW Account fields (Player layouts, read-only): First_Completed_Sign_Up_Date\__c, Last_Completed_Sign_Up_Date_\_c (DateTime).
2. NEW after-save record-triggered flow Sign_Up_After_Save_Update_Player_Activity — entry: Status\__c changed to Completed AND Player_\_c not blank:

    * Call Player_Stamp_Last_Activity with Completion_Date__c (converted per the BUILD-252 date convention note).
    * If First_Completed_Sign_Up\__c blank → set lookup + First_Completed_Sign_Up_Date_\_c.
    * If Last_Completed_Sign_Up_Date__c blank or older → update it.
    * Status branch — only Pending and Inactive Players are eligible for a status write: (1) Pending → Active; (2) Inactive → Active + clear Player_Status_Reason__c; (3) Banned or already Active → status untouched (date fields still stamp).
    
3. Prerequisite: blast-radius check — identify and review **all active automations** that fire on Sign-Up completion or that write to the Player fields this story touches; confirm no conflicts or double-fires (including flows firing on records created already-Completed by data loads); record findings on this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

1. First completed Sign-Up on a Pending Player → Active; lookup, both date fields, Last Activity Date all set; audit fields stamped (via BUILD-251).
2. Completed Sign-Up on an Inactive Player → Active, reason cleared.
3. Must NOT change status on a Banned or already-Active Player (date fields still stamp); must not fire without Player__c or on non-Completed status changes.
4. A second completed Sign-Up never overwrites the First lookup/date; Last date only moves forward.

## Out of scope

* BA/Primary/Secondary Referrer defaulting (awaiting client confirmation — separate ticket).

## Output

Two fields + flow deployed in Partial SB; blast-radius result + API names recorded on this ticket; requirements doc updated; drafted-logic comment on BUILD-177 resolved.
fields.summary: BUILD-253 — Player Status: Activate Player + Sign-Up Stamps on Completed Sign-Up

comments.body:
**Blast-radius check — findings (reviewed against Partial SB metadata in force-app, 2026-09-08)**

No blocking conflicts found. Details and two implementation risks worth addressing below.

**1. Automation already firing on Sign_Up\__c.Status_\_c → Completed**

* `Sign_Up_Before_Save_Stamp_Completion_Date` (Active, before-save, Create+Update) — stamps `Completion_Date__c` when Status = Completed and that field is blank. No field overlap with this story.

* `Sign_Up_Before_Save_Assign_Operator_Partner_Rep_and_Brand_Manager` (Active, before-save) — entry is Status _not equal_ Completed, so it stops running once a Sign-Up completes. Mutually exclusive with the new flow's entry criteria, no overlap.

* DLRS rollup `Sign-Ups - Player Total Completed` (Active, realtime) — counts Sign_Up\__c where Status = Completed into Account.Total_Sign_Upsc via {{Playerc}}. Runs through the DLRS-managed trigger on Sign_Up_\_c (separate from any new flow), and does its own Account update. Not a field conflict, but it is a second automatic write to the Player account in the same transaction — see sequencing note below.

* `Sign_Up_After_Save_Update_Payout_Amount` is Draft (inactive) — no current risk, but flag it if anyone activates it later, since it touches Sign_Up__c after-save on Create+Update.

No other active flow, Process Builder, or Apex trigger reacts to Status\__c = Completed. No Apex trigger logic exists on Sign_Up_\_c or Account beyond the DLRS-generated triggers (`dlrs_Sign_UpTrigger`, `dlrs_AccountTrigger`), which only run the DLRS rollup engine.

**2. Automation writing to the Player fields this story touches**

* `Player_Status__c`: only written today by `SLC_After_Save_Player_DRA_and_Sign_Up` (sets it to "Pending" at Player creation) and the two manual screen flows `Player_Ban_Button` / `Player_Reactivate_Button`. Nothing today automatically flips Pending/Inactive → Active — confirms this story is the first automation to do that.

* `Account_Before_Save_Stamp_Player_Status_Audit` (Active, before-save, BUILD-251) fires on ISCHANGED(Player_Status\__c) for Player-record-type Accounts and stamps {{Player_Status_Set_Datec}} / {{Player_Status_Last_Updated_Byc}}. This will fire automatically whenever the new flow changes Player_Status_\_c — that's expected per the ticket (audit stamping is centralized in BUILD-251), just confirming it will engage correctly since it's a separate before-save flow on the same object.

* `First_Completed_Sign_Up__c`: not referenced by any existing automation. Confirmed unpopulated/untouched today.

* `Last_Activity_Date__c`: the `Player_Stamp_Last_Activity` subflow (BUILD-252, Active) is explicitly documented in its own flow description as the sole writer: "Single writer of Last_Activity_Date__c — new qualifying-activity sources call this subflow, never write the field directly." Confirmed no other flow or Apex writes this field directly. The proposed design in this ticket correctly calls that subflow rather than writing the field itself.

**3. Data-load / insert-time "changed to Completed" behavior**

This org already has a working precedent for exactly this concern: `Sign_Up_Before_Save_Stamp_Completion_Date` avoids relying on IsChanged/doesRequireRecordChangedToMeetCriteria semantics on insert. Instead it uses a direct value filter (Status__c = Completed) plus an idempotency guard (target field IsNull), with recordTriggerType = CreateAndUpdate. That sidesteps any ambiguity about whether "changed" evaluates true on a brand-new record.

Recommendation: build the new `Sign_Up_After_Save_Update_Player_Activity` flow the same way — CreateAndUpdate, entry criteria on the Status\__c value itself (not a bare IsChanged formula), so a data-loaded Sign_Upc created already at Completed fires correctly. Salesforce's documented behavior is that IsChanged/doesRequireRecordChangedToMeetCriteria does treat a populated field on a new record as "changed" (prior value is treated as blank), so this should fire either way — but given the ticket flags this as a specific risk, recommend an explicit sandbox test inserting a Sign_Upc via data load with Statusc = Completed and Player_\_c set, rather than relying on documented behavior alone.

**4. Sequencing risk to watch in the build (new finding, not yet an issue since the flow doesn't exist yet)**

`Player_Stamp_Last_Activity` does its own Get + Update on the Account record (a separate DML, not a $Record-based update). If the new flow also queries the Player Account once, holds it in memory to set Player_Status\__c / First_Completed_Sign_Up_\_c / date fields, and performs its own "Update Records" using that in-memory copy _after_ calling the subflow, that later update could overwrite the Last_Activity_Date\__c value the subflow just set (stale in-memory copy, DML ordering conflict). Recommend either: re-query the Account after calling the subflow before the flow's own update, call the subflow last so its write is final, or scope the flow's own Update Records action to only the specific fields it owns (excluding Last_Activity_Date_\_c) rather than passing the whole record.

**5. Minor documentation flag (not a blast-radius conflict)**

The existing `First_Completed_Sign_Up__c` field description reads "Set automatically when their status flips from Pending to Active" — narrower than the approved design here, which also stamps the lookup/date for Inactive → Active, and stamps the date fields (not the status) even for Banned/already-Active players. Worth updating that field description when the two new date fields are created, so it doesn't mislead the next person who reads it.

**Bottom line:** no active automation conflicts with or double-fires against this story's entry criteria. Proceed with the proposed solution; just apply the CreateAndUpdate + value-filter entry criteria pattern (not bare IsChanged) and watch the Account DML sequencing between the flow's own update and the Player_Stamp_Last_Activity call.

**Changes made:** 

| **Metadata Name** | **Metadata Type** | **Action** | **Notes** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sign_Up_After_Save_Update_Player_Activity | Flow | New Component |

| Account.First_Completed_Sign_Up_Date__c | Customfield | New Component |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Account.Last_Completed_Sign_Up_Date__c | Customfield | New Component |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Player_Account_Page1 | Flexipage | Update Component | Added Account.First_Completed_Sign_Up_Date\__c & Account.Last_Completed_Sign_Up_Date_\_c |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WT_PersonAccount_Player_Read | PermissionSet |

| Added Account.First_Completed_Sign_Up_Date\__c & Account.Last_Completed_Sign_Up_Date_\_c |
| --- |
| WT_PersonAccount_Player_Edit | PermissionSet |

| Added Account.First_Completed_Sign_Up_Date\__c & Account.Last_Completed_Sign_Up_Date_\_c |
| --- |

**Testing:** Validated in sandbox. Working as expected.

**Scenario 1:** Pending Player > Completed a Sign Up > Active Player

**Scenario 2:** Inactive Player > Migrate Sign Ups - 250 Test Data; thread limit to 12> Player Status Activated. 

**Scenario 3:** Player is Banned > Complete a Sign Up > No Status Update; Last Activity & Last Completed Sign Up Updated

fields.description:
## Summary

Whenever qualifying activity occurs (v1: a completed Sign-Up), the related Player's Last Activity Date updates to the most recent activity date — through one reusable subflow that every current and future activity source calls.

## Context

BUILD-178's status automation runs off Account.Last_Activity_Date__c — the date of the player's most recent qualifying activity. The definition of "qualifying activity" will grow (today: completed Sign-Ups; later possibly redeposits or CMS logins). To keep future sources from each re-implementing date logic, exactly one subflow owns writes to this field.

## Current state

Account.Last_Activity_Date\__c (Date) exists on the Player Person Account, with help text referencing the 90-day threshold — nothing populates it. Sign-Ups link to Players via Sign_Upc.Player_\_c.

## Proposed solution

NEW autolaunched subflow Player_Stamp_Last_Activity — inputs: PlayerId (Text), ActivityDate (Date). Logic: if the Player's current Last_Activity_Date\__c is blank or older than ActivityDate → update it; otherwise no-op. The date never moves backwards. Flow description must read: "Single writer of Last_Activity_Date_\_c — new qualifying-activity sources call this subflow, never write the field directly." First caller: the BUILD-253 flow.

**Date convention note.** Last_Activity_Date\__c stays a **Date** deliberately — the 90-day threshold is a calendar-day rule, so the scheduled check in BUILD-254 compares whole days with no time-zone ambiguity. Callers converting a DateTime source (e.g., Completion_Date_\_c) to the ActivityDate input must convert to the calendar date in the org time zone (ET); developer to verify a completion near midnight doesn't land on the wrong day.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A newer ActivityDate (or a blank field) updates the field; an older ActivityDate is a no-op.
2. Re-running with an identical date performs no DML.
3. Bulk-safe when invoked from a record-triggered flow processing 200 records.

## Output

Subflow deployed in Partial SB; API name + registered-caller list recorded on this ticket; requirements doc updated.

Summary

Direct deals now have multiple sources, so two BetMGM-Direct-ON deals can differ only by source — the current name format can't tell them apart in list views. Solution: the Deal Name flow appends -{Source_Code__c} after Vertical (all deals, only when Source is set), keeping -TEST as the final token — e.g. ON-BETMGM-DIRECT-CASINO-S. Extends the format from BUILD-117/BUILD-125.

Current state

Flow Deal_Before_Save_Set_Deal_Name sets Name via formula DealNameFormat: {Market_State_Code_c|country}{Operator Name}{Partner_Codec}-{Vertical} uppercased, then -TEST if Test_Deal_c. Example: ON-BETMGM-GD-CASINO. Fires on create and update with no entry filter → Name restamps whenever deal makeup changes (decided behavior; CMS keys on External Deal ID, not Name).

Proposed solution

  1. Modify DealNameFormat to append -{Source_Code_c} (from BUILD-246) after Vertical, only when Source_Code_c is non-blank, keeping TEST as the final token: {geo}{OPERATOR}{PARTNER_CODE}{VERTICAL}[-{S}][-TEST]

  2. "Direct" remains spelled out in full (explicit Aug 25 decision — no -D shortening).

Acceptance criteria

  1. Existing before-save trigger on create/update; no new trigger.

  2. Deal with Source=Shurzy → name ends -S; suffix applies to all deals (any partner), not only Direct.

  3. Source blank → name identical to today's format, no trailing hyphen.

  4. Test deal with Source → …-S-TEST, not …-TEST-S.

  5. Re-saving an unchanged Deal produces the same Name (idempotent).

Out of scope

  • External Deal ID (BUILD-247).

  • Requiring Source (BUILD-249).

comments.body:
Updated Formula in this flow: Deal - After Save - Set Deal Name https://nosoftware-nosoftware-7430--partialsb.sandbox.lightning.force.com/builder_platform_interaction/flowBuilder.app?flowId=301WJ000011YdkIYAS

UPPER(

BLANKVALUE(

IF( LEN({!$Record.Market_State_Code__c}) > 0,

{!$Record.Market_State_Code__c},

IF( {!$Record.Market_Country_Code__c} = 'US & CA', 'USCA',

{!$Record.Market_Country_Code__c} )

), 'NOMKT')

& '-' & BLANKVALUE({!$Record.Operator__r.Name}, 'NOOP')

& '-' & BLANKVALUE({!$Record.Partner_r.Partner_Code_c}, 'NOPT')

& '-' & TEXT({!$Record.Vertical__c})

)

& IF( LEN({

$Record.Source_Code__c}, '' )

& IF( {!$Record.Test_Deal__c}, '-TEST', '' )

  • Formula above also makes some improvements on handling blank values for operator/partner,etc. and renamed the flow to After Save as it was previously named Before Save incorrectly.

Heads-up on the Source_Code__c reference (2026-09-08)

The formula in this ticket references {!$Record.Source_Code__c}, which is safe as written — Deal_Before_Save_Set_Deal_Name is actually an after-save flow despite its "Before Save" label, and after-save flows read recalculated formula fields fine.

It becomes a silent defect if that flow is ever converted to before-save (the mislabelled trigger type is worth its own clone-and-rebuild ticket). Before-save flows cannot read same-record formula fields — on insert the value is blank, on update it is the pre-update value. If the conversion happens, replace the reference with an in-flow CASE, mirroring fxSourceCode in the External Deal ID flow but without its NOSRC fallback (the placeholder belongs in the id, not the Name). Otherwise every new deal name silently loses its Source suffix.

Related: BUILD-272 — Deal: Makeup dedupe key and duplicate block, which extends that External Deal ID flow.

fields.description:
## Summary

Whenever a Player's Player_Status\__c changes — from any source: manual UI edit, screen flow, record-triggered or scheduled automation, or data load — the system stamps Player_Status_Set_Datec and Player_Status_Last_Updated_By_\_c.

## Context

Every other story in this epic (BUILD-178) writes Player status, and statuses can also change by hand (e.g., the unban path in BUILD-255) or via data updates. Rather than each automation stamping audit fields itself — and manual edits slipping through unstamped — one before-save flow on Account owns the stamping for every path. The other children rely on this story and do no stamping of their own.

## Current state

Player_Status_Set_Date\__c (DateTime) exists. Player_Status_Last_Updated_By_\_c exists as a **Lookup(User)** — a lookup is unnecessary for an audit field and will be replaced with Text. Lookup fields cannot be converted in place; the field must be deleted and recreated.

## Proposed solution

1. REPLACE Account.Player_Status_Last_Updated_By__c: delete the Lookup(User) field (currently unpopulated) and recreate it as **Text**, same label ("Status Last Updated By"), read-only on layouts.
2. NEW before-save record-triggered flow Account_Before_Save_Stamp_Player_Status_Audit — entry: Player record type AND Player_Status\__c changed. Stamps Player_Status_Set_Datec = now and Player_Status_Last_Updated_By_\_c = the running user's name. Automated contexts (e.g., the BUILD-254 scheduled flow) will stamp "Automated Process" — this is expected and desirable for the audit trail.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A status change via manual UI edit, screen flow, record-triggered flow, scheduled flow, or data load stamps both fields.
2. Account edits that do not change Player_Status__c leave both fields untouched.
3. Scheduled/automated status changes stamp "Automated Process" as the updater.
4. Bulk-safe at 200+ records.

## Output

Recreated field + flow deployed in Partial SB; API names recorded on this ticket; requirements doc updated.

fields.description:
## Summary

When a Sign-Up's Status first becomes Completed, the system stamps the completion date/time on the Sign-Up — once, permanently.

## Context

Player status automation (BUILD-178 epic) turns on the moment a Sign-Up is completed, and the 90-day inactivity clock is measured from completion moments. Sign_Up__c has no field recording when Status became Completed — this story creates that timestamp. Prerequisite for every other story in the epic.

## Current state

Sign-Up completion runs through the Screen_Sign_Up_Complete screen flow → Complete_Sign_Up autolaunched flow, which writes deposit/first-bet fields and Status\__c — no timestamp. Status_\_c can also be set to Completed directly by a data load.

## Proposed solution

1. NEW field Sign_Up\__c.Completion_Date_\_c — DateTime, read-only on layouts, help text: "Set automatically when Status first becomes Completed."
2. Stamp the field exactly once, at the moment Status first becomes Completed, covering **both** the screen-flow path and direct record updates/data loads. Suggested approach: a before-save record-triggered flow (Sign_Up_Before_Save_Stamp_Completion_Date) — it covers every path without touching Complete_Sign_Up. Developer may adjust the implementation if there's a better fit, as long as the acceptance criteria hold.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Completing a Sign-Up via the screen flow or a data load/record update stamps the field, once.
2. The value never changes after first stamp — editing a Completed record, or Archived → reactivated → Completed again, keeps the original.
3. Status changes to any non-Completed value do not stamp.

## Output

Field + flow deployed in Partial SB; API names recorded on this ticket; requirements doc updated.

## Summary

Ops bans a Player through a button that requires a reason and sets Status to Banned. Unbanning is a manual status edit restricted to Ops/Admins — reps can't edit Player Status at all.

## Context

Banned is the one manual Player status — the automation in this epic (BUILD-178) never sets or clears it. The client asked for a controlled path: a **Ban button** on the Player that captures the reason, and unbanning restricted to Ops/Admins so reps can't flip statuses by hand.

## Current state

Account.Ban_Reason\__c and Account.Ban_Notesc exist, unused by any UI. Player_Status_\_c is editable by anyone with the field on-layout — no restriction. A Referrer_Ban_Button screen flow already exists for the Referrer ban path — mirror its structure, naming, and UX (warning text, required reason, notes) for consistency.

## Proposed solution

1. NEW screen flow + quick action Ban Player on Account (Player record type): requires Ban_Reason\__c (optional Ban_Notesc), sets Player_Status_\_c = Banned. (Audit stamping via BUILD-251.)
2. Unban = manually editing Player_Status__c on the record. Restrict field edit access to Ops/Admin profiles/permission sets — align with the WT permission set group model (confirm which PSG at grooming).
3. Rep-facing layouts: Player_Status__c read-only.
4. At grooming, confirm who can run the Ban action and the flow's run context: with rep edit access removed at field level, either restrict the quick action's visibility to Ops/Admin, or run the flow in system context if reps should be able to ban.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Ban action requires a reason, sets Banned, audit fields stamped (via BUILD-251).
2. Banned Players are ignored by the BUILD-253 and BUILD-254 automations (their ACs cover it; regression-check here).
3. Rep users cannot edit Player_Status__c; Ops/Admin users can (unban path) — and a manual unban still stamps the audit fields (via BUILD-251).
4. Ban action on an already-Banned Player is a no-op or blocked with a clear message.

## Output

Screen flow, quick action, and permission changes deployed in Partial SB; PSG used recorded on this ticket; requirements doc updated.

fields.description:
Problem

Clicking Log Sign Up advances Status__c from New to In Progress even when nothing was entered. The silent status change with zero data is unintuitive (Emily). The "accept with no info" intent is dropped.

Current state

The Log Sign Up screen flow sets Status__c = In Progress unconditionally on completion.

Proposed solution

In the Log Sign Up flow, compare screen inputs to current record values.

Set Status__c = In Progress only if ANY field was entered/changed.

If no changes detected, show a screen letting the user know that the record will not move to In Progress unless any of the fields are filled in.

* User should be able to close the screen or go back and enter any info to update the record to In Progress. Closing the screen without any changes should not update the record status to In Progress.

Otherwise save without status change (record stays New).

Acceptance criteria

Field set should include First Wager Date being added to the Log Sign Up flow as per BUILD-242.

Trigger — Log Sign Up screen flow finish, on Sign_Up__c.

Positive — any single field entered or changed → status becomes In Progress.

Negative — popup opened and finished with nothing entered → status stays New. Popup cancelled → no change at all.

Idempotency — running Log Sign Up on an already-In Progress record never regresses status to New.

Out of scope

Minimum-required-fields gating (alternative rejected; Emily chose "any field edited").

Complete-gating (C2) unaffected.

Test data

One New Sign-Up logged with only Referrer filled (→ In Progress); one New Sign-Up logged with nothing (→ stays New).

Source

Emily doc comment 2026-08-28: "let's go with original ask, 'any field edited' will advance the record to in progress." [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LOMrG0-0JchyP9wHrV4hMlBqh-gMq8YxknpySd5OJjY/edit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LOMrG0-0JchyP9wHrV4hMlBqh-gMq8YxknpySd5OJjY/edit)

## Problem

E-Transfer Email shows blank on Sign-Up records. The field maps from Player's E-Transfer Email field, which never receives data — the email CMS sends in the SLC payload IS the e-transfer email, landing in PersonEmail.

## Current state

Player carries three email fields: PersonEmail (populated via SLC), Secondary_Email__c, and E-Transfer Email (unpopulated, off the Player layout). Sign-Up displays the E-Transfer field, so it is always blank.

## Proposed solution

1. Replace E-Transfer Email with the Email field on the Sign-Up layout/component.
2. Remove E-Transfer Email from any remaining layouts, popups, and SLC field mappings.
3. Do NOT delete the fields (see open question).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Sign-Up record view shows the Player/SLC email under a single Email display.
2. Negative: no layout, screen flow, or list view still references E-Transfer Email.
3. Idempotency: n/a (display change).

## Out of scope

* CMS API change to send a distinct e-transfer email (rejected option).

## Open question (non-blocking)

Deprecate the E-Transfer Email fields on Player/SLC/Sign-Up now, or keep dormant in case players can later set a separate e-transfer email in CMS?

## Source

Emily doc comment 2026-08-28: "the email we send you is the e-transfer email… Player email = signup e-transfer email." [Feedback doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LOMrG0-0JchyP9wHrV4hMlBqh-gMq8YxknpySd5OJjY/edit)

## Problem

Fraud flagging is only available for In Progress and Completed Sign-Ups. Emily + Lina confirmed New-status records must also be flaggable.

## Current state

Flag_Sign_Up screen flow (reason code + notes) is exposed only at In Progress/Completed. New records have no flag entry point.

## Proposed solution

1. Expose the Flag action (button + Flag_Sign_Up flow) on New-status Sign-Ups.
2. Reuse the existing reason-code + notes modal and Fraud_Review_Status__c lifecycle — no new flow.

## Acceptance criteria (draft — item 3 blocked pending answers below)

1. Positive — a New Sign-Up can be flagged with reason code + notes, identical modal to In Progress.
2. Negative — flagging does not advance the record to In Progress.
3. BLOCKED: post-flag status behaviour, list-view visibility, ops review path.

## Blocked on (client-facing question list)

1. Once a New Sign-Up is flagged — does it stay New, or move to Archived?
2. Should flagged New Sign-Ups hide from rep list views?
3. Do they enter the same ops fraud-review workflow as In Progress/Completed/Archived flags?

## Source

Emily doc comment, resolved thread 2026-08-28: Lina confirmed status New should have the ability to be marked as fraud. [Feedback doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LOMrG0-0JchyP9wHrV4hMlBqh-gMq8YxknpySd5OJjY/edit)
fields.summary: BUILD-245 — Sign-Up: Enable fraud flagging at New status

comments.body:
Added:

Record Status>Equals>New

(1 OR 2 OR 4) AND 3

Questions answered in 09/01 sync—

**Q1 — Status of a flagged New sign-up. New scope added.**

* Fraud confirmed, no payment sent → move status from New to Archived.
* Fraud confirmed, payment sent → do not change status. Set a new "Write-off" checkbox instead.
* Fraud dismissed → return the record to its prior status. Remove the flag only.
* New scope: add a "Write-off" checkbox. Confirm if a "Payment Sent" field exists. Add logic to set Write-off = true when fraud is confirmed and Payment Sent = true.

**Q2 — Hide flagged New sign-ups from rep list views.** 

* Archived records already drop off rep list views. This covers confirmed-fraud records.

**Q3 — Same fraud-review workflow as later-stage flags. RESOLVED.**

* Yes. New-status flags follow the same suspected → confirmed/dismissed path as other statuses.

The related list is called “Accounts (Brand Ambassador)” for now.

Emily's Sep 15 follow-up asked two things about the "Accounts (Brand Ambassador)" related list: will it be renamed, and will it be searchable.

Searchable: confirmed it isn't currently. The Related List - Single component on the Brand Ambassador page only exposes Related List Type = Default or Enhanced List, no direct search toggle. Needs a check with Cedrick on dependencies before scoping this as a quick change.

Replied to Emily flagging the searchability constraint and asking whether that changes if the BAs would use this list at all — **holding off on investigating the rename until we hear back, since her original note was "not sure if BAs would even use this."**
Met with Emily 09/28 and we’re not going to build this related list as she doesn’t find it to be useful to the BA’s with the lack of customization

## Summary

Deal names and External Deal IDs need a source shortcode (Aug 25 sync decision), and two flows need the same Source→code mapping — without a single source of truth the CASE logic gets duplicated and drifts. **Solution: one formula field on Deal that translates the Source picklist into its shortcode, referenced by both naming flows (BUILD-247, BUILD-248).**

## Current state

Deal\__c.Source_\_c exists (picklist: Shurzy, Vectiq, WagerTech, PredictiveX; optional; blank on all existing Deals). No shortcode field or mapping exists anywhere in the org. Formula chosen over CMDT deliberately: 4 rarely-changing values, keeps both naming flows formula-only (no added DML/SOQL); revisit CMDT only if the source list grows.

## Proposed solution

1. Create Deal\__c.Source_Codec — Formula (Text): {{CASE(TEXT(Source_\_c), "Shurzy","S", "Vectiq","V", "WagerTech","WT", "PredictiveX","P", "")}}
2. Automation-only field: not on page layouts, available to reports.
3. Field description must state that Source_Code__c — the price of skipping CMDT.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Each of the 4 picklist values returns its mapped code (S, V, WT, P).
2. Blank Source__c returns "" (empty string), not an error.
3. A new picklist value not yet in the CASE returns "" (known limitation, covered by the field description).

## Out of scope

* Flow changes (BUILD-247, BUILD-248).
* CMDT-based mapping.

# RF-1 (support): Primary/Secondary Referrals Roll-Up Automation

_Populate Referrer's Primary Referrals and Secondary Referrals Count fields via Flow, since the Sign Up → Referrer relationship uses Lookup fields, not Master-Detail, so native Roll-Up Summary fields are not available._

### FIELDS

* Primary Referrals — Number(0), read-only via page layout/FLS, on Referrer (already exists per BUILD-185; confirm it is a plain Number field, not Roll-Up Summary)
* Secondary Referrals — Number(0), read-only via page layout/FLS, on Referrer (same)

### IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

* Two Record-Triggered Flows on Sign Up (After Save: create, update, delete) — one for Primary Referrer, one for Secondary Referrer

* On create, update, or delete, recalculate the affected Referrer's count by querying and counting matching Sign Up records fresh each time, rather than incrementing/decrementing, to avoid drift under bulk operations
* On update where the referrer lookup value changed, recalculate both the old and new Referrer's counts

* Assumes either lookup can be blank on a given Sign Up

* Ruled out converting to Master-Detail for this reason — Master-Detail fields cannot be null. Discussed with Taryn in chat, Aug 26, 2026 — not from a transcript.

### NOTES

* Provenance: none — this ticket was opened directly from a build blocker Taryn hit while working [BUILD-185 — Referrer: Object + Core Status](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1217693311564006/f/). Primary Referrals and Secondary Referrals could not be built as native Roll-Up Summary fields because the underlying relationship is a Lookup, not Master-Detail.
* Exact API names for the Primary Referrer / Secondary Referrer lookups on Sign Up not yet confirmed — verify neither is a Master-Detail relationship before building.

### SOURCE

* No user-story doc citation — created directly from a build blocker on [BUILD-185 — Referrer: Object + Core Status](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1217693311564006/f/), discussed with Taryn in chat, Aug 26, 2026.
* Dependents: [BUILD-185 — Referrer: Object + Core Status](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1217693311564006/f/) (blocked on this ticket's automation)
* Owner (proposed): Taryn Reithofer

fields.summary: BUILD-238 — Referrer: Primary/Secondary Referrals Roll-Up Automation

comments.body:
**Build status: in progress, paused for review. Flow: "Sign Up - After Save - Update Primary Referrals on Referrer"**

[https://nosoftware-nosoftware-7430--partialsb.sandbox.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/FlowRecord/2aFWJ0000047PAg2AM/view](https://nosoftware-nosoftware-7430--partialsb.sandbox.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/FlowRecord/2aFWJ0000047PAg2AM/view) (version 2)

**Start**

* Object: Sign Up
* Trigger: A record is created or updated
* Optimize for: Actions and Related Records

**Fields created this session, both on Account:**

* Primary Referrals — Number(18,0), field-level security visible/not editable on all profiles, added to the Referrer page layout. Expected API name: Primary_Referrals__c
* Secondary Referrals — same spec. Expected API name: Secondary_Referrals__c

Both should be spot-checked in Object Manager to confirm exact API names before Secondary Referrals flow is built, since they were not re-verified after creation.

**Decision 1 — "New Primary Referrer Not Null" (API: New_Primary_Referrer_Not_Null)**

* Outcome "Has Primary Referrer" (API: Has_Primary_Referrer): Resource = Referrer (Referrer\__c), Triggering Sign_Up_\_c version. Operator = Is Null. Value = {!$GlobalConstant.False}
* Default Outcome: no referrer set

**"Has Primary Referrer" path:**

* Get Records "Get Sign Ups for Referrer" — Object: Sign Up. Condition: Referrer\__c Equals {!$Record.Referrer_\_c}. Store: automatically store all fields, all records.
* Loop "Look Through Sign Ups" — Collection: {!Get_Sign_Ups_for_Referrer}. Direction: first item to last item.
* Assignment "Add to Count" (inside For Each) — countVar: Add, 1.
* Variable countVar — Number, 0 decimal places, default 0, not available for input/output.
* Update Records "Update Referrer Primary Referrals" (After Last) — How to Find Records: "Update records related to the sign up record that triggered the flow." Related Records: Referrer (Referrer\__r), Triggering Sign_Up_\_c. Condition Requirements: None — Update All Related Records. Field Values: Primary Referrals = {!countVar}.

Both this path and the Default Outcome path merge and feed into Decision 2.

**Decision 2 — "Referrer Changed On Update" (API: Referrer_Changed_On_Update)**

* Outcome "Old Referrer Needs Recalc" (API: Old_Referrer_Needs_Recalc), All Conditions Are Met (AND):

* Condition 1: Referrer (Referrer\__c), Prior Values of Triggering Sign_Up_\_c version. Operator: Is Null. Value: {!$GlobalConstant.False}
* Condition 2: Referrer (Referrer\__c), Prior Values version. Operator: Does Not Equal. Value: Referrer (Referrerc), Triggering Sign_Up_\_c version.

* Default Outcome: goes straight to End.

**"Old Referrer Needs Recalc" path — NOT YET COMPLETE:**

* Get Records "Get Sign Ups for Old Referrer" — Object: Sign Up. Condition: Referrer\__c Equals {!$RecordPrior.Referrer_\_c}. Store: automatically store all fields, all records. Done.
* Loop "Loop Through Old Referrer Sign Ups" — Collection: {!Get_Sign_Ups_for_Old_Referrer}. Direction: first item to last item. Done.
* Assignment "Add to Old Count" (inside For Each) — oldCountVar: Add, 1. Done.
* Variable oldCountVar — Number, 0 decimal places, default 0, not available for input/output. Done.
* Get Records "Get Old Referrer Account" (After Last) — Object: Account. Intended condition: Id Equals {!$Record\__Prior.Referrer_\_c}. BLOCKED: the standard Id field does not appear in this org's field search here, or in the equivalent Update Records screen earlier. Last thing tried, not confirmed: switching this element to "Update records related to..." using a Prior Values relationship path, the same shortcut that worked for the new Referrer branch.
* Not yet built: Assignment to set the fetched old Referrer record's Primary Referrals field to {!oldCountVar}.
* Not yet built: Update Records to save that record, likely via "Use the IDs and all field values from a record or record collection."

**Explicitly out of scope for this flow:** record deletion. Salesforce does not allow one Record-Triggered Flow trigger to cover create, update, and delete together. A second, delete-only flow is still needed.

**Once complete:** save, activate, and test against a real Sign Up before relying on the counts. The Secondary Referrals flow should be built by cloning this one with Save As and swapping field references, rather than rebuilt element by element.
After discussing with Kobi, these rollups can be completed by a DLRS. Screenshots from the two created and both tested ✅
