# RF-12b: Ban Button — Confirm Reason/Notes Capture

### IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

* A Ban button on the Referrer record (Account, Referrer record type) opens a screen flow that captures a Ban Reason, Ban Notes, and an optional "Flag related Player record" checkbox.
* Ban Reason is a required single-select field.
* Ban Notes is a required free-text field.
* On submission, the flow sets Referrer Status = Banned on the record.
* On submission, the flow moves all unpaid payouts (Status = New or Logged) on this Referrer to Hold. Payouts already at Paid are not affected.
* If "Flag related Player record" is checked, the flow sets the related Player's Review Required and Review Reason fields (see BUILD-177).
* Full automation detail (payout-Hold logic, Flag Player behavior) is built and tracked in [BUILD-196 — Referrer: Ban Automation](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1217693254043092/f/) — this ticket documents the confirmed Ban Reason values and the decision to build the button.

### FIELDS

* Ban Reason — Radio button (single-select), required. Values: Under Investigation, Confirmed Fraud, Network Policy Violation, Associated with Banned Network, Other.
* Ban Notes — Text (long text recommended), required.

### NOTES

* Provenance: raised in the Aug 24 Kobi/Taryn Weekly Planning sync; confirmed in the Aug 25 Wagertech <> Jumpr Weekly Sync.

fields.description:
**DONE 2026-08-20 by Kobi.** Recorded so the steps are repeatable — this is the setup every new Brand Ambassador needs before deals or sign-ups can be assigned to them.

## What was done

Applied to **Alexander Kovacevic** and **Andy Bhiekham** in the Partial sandbox:

1. **Rep External ID** (`User.Rep_External_Id__c`) — Alex `1686734`, Andy `1507535`. Values supplied by WagerTech on the Aug-18 deal assignment sheet. Unique, case-sensitive external ID.
2. **Rep Slug** (`User.Rep_Slug__c`) — Alex `akresearch`, Andy `alresearch`.
3. **Manager** — Emily Vandenberg set as manager on both User records.
4. **Permission set group** — assigned **WT Rep** to both.

## Why step 4 matters — this one bit us

The `WagerTech Sales Rep` **profile grants no access at all** to `Sign_Up__c`, `Deal__c` or `Deal_Rep_Assignment__c`. It covers Account, Contact, Opportunity, Order, Case, Campaign, Contract, Product2, Pricebook2 and Graphics_Pack_Example\__c only. Every WagerTech object is granted through the {{WT_\*}} permission sets.

Without the group assigned, the Sign-Up remap failed with:

```
TRANSFER_REQUIRES_READ: The new owner must have read permission
```

Chain: setting `Sign_Up__c.Deal_Rep_Assignment__c` fires the before-save flow _Sign Up - Assign Operator, Partner, Rep and Brand Manager_, which sets `Rep__c`. That fires _Sign Up - Owner set to the Brand Ambassador_, which sets `OwnerId = Rep__c`. Salesforce rejects the ownership transfer because the incoming owner cannot read the object. The load reports a hard error, not a silent skip.

## Runbook — do this for every new BA

1. Set `Rep_External_Id__c` from the value the CMS will send in `rep_external_id`. Must match exactly — it is case-sensitive.
2. Set `Rep_Slug__c` to the rep's agency slug.
3. Set Manager.
4. Assign the **WT Rep** permission set group.
5. Verify before loading any Deal Rep Assignments — see query below.

## Verification query

```
SELECT Assignee.Name, Assignee.Rep_External_Id__c, Assignee.Rep_Slug__c,
```

```
PermissionSetGroup.DeveloperName, PermissionSet.Name
```

```
FROM PermissionSetAssignment
```

```
WHERE Assignee.Profile.Name = 'WagerTech Sales Rep'
```

```
ORDER BY Assignee.Name
```

## Open follow-up

**Nothing assigns the WT Rep group automatically.** Every new BA lands in the broken state until someone remembers this card. Options: assign the group via a flow on User create, bake it into an onboarding checklist, or move the WagerTech objects onto the profile. Related to BUILD-01 (4-tier permission model). Worth a decision before go-live — a rep who cannot own their own Sign-Ups is a hard stop, not a cosmetic issue.

_Context: this surfaced during the 2026-08-20 Deal + DRA load (15 Deals, 21 DRAs) from the client's assignment sheet._

# PL-15: Total Sign-Ups (DLRS Rollup)

_Give reps and Ops a quick count of how many completed Sign Ups a player has, directly on the record._

### AUTOMATION

* A Number field on Player (Total Sign-Ups) is maintained by a DLRS (Declarative Lookup Rollup Summary) rollup — not a native Salesforce Roll-Up Summary field

* Counts completed Sign Ups only — the rollup's Relationship Criteria filters to Sign Up Status = Completed
* DLRS is required specifically because Sign Up relates to Player via a standard Lookup, not Master-Detail — native Roll-Up Summary fields aren't available on Lookup relationships

### IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

* Build using DLRS, not a native Roll-Up Summary field. Support is available if issues come up during setup.

### NOTES

* Provenance: new item raised in the Aug 24 Kobi/Taryn Weekly Planning sync — not part of the original Player Record User Stories doc's PL-1 through PL-14 story map. Numbered PL-15 as a natural extension.
* Field itself (Total_Sign_Ups__c, Number, 0 decimal places, default 0) must exist on Account before the DLRS rollup definition can target it.
* DLRS rollup definition: Parent Object = Account, Child Object = Sign Up, Relationship Field = the Sign Up → Player lookup, Relationship Criteria = Status equals Completed, Field to Aggregate = Name (placeholder, irrelevant for Count), Aggregate Operation = Count, Aggregate Result Field = Total_Sign_Ups__c, Calculation Mode = Realtime, Active = checked.
* Run DLRS's full recalculation after activating, to backfill existing Players rather than only counting Sign Ups going forward.

### SOURCE

* Aug 24 Kobi/Taryn Weekly Planning — [transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qB7cUeJGFs_SZba9NX5R9MWKzOj8yTetmWTWoqY3gw8/edit), verified.
* Dependencies: [BUILD-173 — Player: Core Details fields](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1217684264652851/f/), and [✓ POC-10 — Create Sign-Up object and fields](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1216276872010067/f/) (need Sign Up's Status field and Player lookup).
* Owner (proposed): Taryn Reithofer

# PL-5: Ban Status + Banner (simplified)

_Simplified ban handling on the Player record — a manual status flip plus a top-of-record banner, with no persisted restriction-detail fields._

### FIELDS

* Player Status — Picklist (existing field, already covered under PL-1/BUILD-173)

* Set to Banned manually by Ops. No separate ban-reason fields get persisted on the Player record.

* Ban Banner — Page component, not a stored field

* Shown at the top of the record when Player Status = Banned, e.g. "This player is banned — see Sign Ups for details."

* Do not build the Restriction Detail fields

## Objective

Every Deal receives a unique External Deal ID on creation without manual entry.

## Dependencies

* All Operator Accounts have `Operator_External_ID__c` populated (Aug-13 external ID load)

* All Partner Accounts have `Partner_Code__c` populated

* BUILD-170 (Vertical: add Prediction Markets) — included in the vertical CASE below

* `HIGH5-GD-US-SC-2` renumbered to `HIGH5-GD-US-SC-002` in the Deal load data before the Deal load runs

## Implementation Requirements

**Field checks (no field changes)**

* External Deal ID — `External_Deal_ID__c` — Text(80), Unique, External ID — confirm Case Insensitive is set

* Confirm `External_Deal_ID__c` is not marked required on the classic Deal Layout. The New/Edit modal still uses that layout, and layout-required blocks the save before any flow runs.

**Flow: Deal - Before Save - Set External Deal ID**

* Object — `Deal__c`

* Trigger — Before Save (Fast Field Update)

* Run on — Create and Update

* Entry criteria — `External_Deal_ID__c` is blank

* The flow must never overwrite a populated `External_Deal_ID__c`

**Formula resource 1 — fxStateCode — Text**

Copy the CASE body verbatim from the existing `Deal__c.Market_State_Code__c` formula field, changing only the CASE subject to `TEXT({!$Record.Market_State__c})` and dropping the outer IF(ISPICKVAL(...)) wrapper. 69 state/province branches, empty-string default. Do not retype the codes — copy them, so the two stay identical.

**Formula resource 2 — fxBaseKey — Text**

```
BLANKVALUE(
```

```
SUBSTITUTE({!$Record.Operator__r.Operator_External_ID__c}, "OP-", ""),
```

```
"NOOP")
```

```

```

```
BLANKVALUE({!$Record.Partner__r.Partner_Code__c}, "NOPT")
```

```

```

```
BLANKVALUE(
```

```
IF( ISBLANK({!fxStateCode}),
```

```
CASE(TEXT({!$Record.Market_Country__c}),
```

```
"United States",          "US",
```

```
"Canada",                 "CA",
```

```
"United States & Canada", "USCA",
```

```
""),
```

```
IF( TEXT({!$Record.Market_Country__c}) = "United States",
```

```
"US-" & {!fxStateCode},
```

```
IF( TEXT({!$Record.Market_Country__c}) = "United States & Canada",
```

```

```

```
{!fxStateCode} ))
```

```

```

```

```

```
CASE(TEXT({!$Record.Vertical__c}),
```

```
"Casino",             "CAS",
```

```
"Sportsbook",         "SB",
```

```
"Social Casino",      "SC",
```

```

```

```
"Sweepstakes",        "SWP",
```

```
"Prediction Markets", "PM",
```

```
"XXX")
```

**Formula resource 3 — fxNextSuffix — Number, Decimal Places 0**

```
IF( {!Get_Highest_Match.External_Deal_ID__c} = {!fxBaseKey},
```

```
2,
```

```
VALUE(
```

```
RIGHT( {!Get_Highest_Match.External_Deal_ID__c},
```

```
LEN({!Get_Highest_Match.External_Deal_ID__c}) - LEN({!fxBaseKey}) - 1 )
```

Decimal Places must be 0. At 2, TEXT() returns "2.00" and the padding produces a malformed suffix.

**Formula resource 4 — fxFinalId — Text**

```
IF( ISBLANK({!Get_Highest_Match.Id}),
```

```

```

```
IF( {!fxNextSuffix} > 999,
```

```
{!fxBaseKey} & "-OVERFLOW",
```

```
{!fxBaseKey} & "-" & RIGHT("00" & TEXT({!fxNextSuffix}), 3)
```

```
)
```

```

```

**Element 1 — Get Records — Get_Highest_Match**

* Object — `Deal__c`

* Condition Requirements — All Conditions Are Met

* Filter — `External_Deal_ID__c` · Starts With · `{!fxBaseKey`}

* Sort Order — Descending

* Sort By — `External_Deal_ID__c`

* How Many Records — Only the first record

* How to Store — Automatically store all fields

**Element 2 — Assignment — Set_External_Deal_Id**

* `{!$Record.External_Deal_ID__c`} Equals `{!fxFinalId`}

Connect Start → Get_Highest_Match → Set_External_Deal_Id → End. No Update Records element — before-save flows assign directly to $Record.

**Segment reference**

* Operator — `Operator__r.Operator_External_ID__c` minus `OP-` → BETMGM, HOLLYWOODCASINO

* Partner — `Partner__r.Partner_Code__c` → D, C, CTM, GD, DIRECT

* Market, Canada + province — fxStateCode → ON, AB

* Market, US + state — "US-" + fxStateCode → US-NJ, US-IL

* Market, US & CA + state — "USCA-" + fxStateCode → USCA-NJ

* Market, no state — Market Country → US, CA, USCA

* Vertical — `Vertical__c` → CAS, SB, SC, DFS, SWP, PM

* Collision suffix — highest existing + 1, zero-padded to 3 → -002, -003, -100

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Creating a Deal with Operator, Partner, Market Country, Market State and Vertical populated sets `External_Deal_ID__c` on save with no user input.

1. BetMGM / GDC / Canada / Ontario / Casino → `BETMGM-GD-ON-CAS`

1. BetRivers / Catena / United States / New Jersey / Casino → `BETRIVERS-CTM-US-NJ-CAS`

1. DraftKings / Cipher / United States / (no state) / Sportsbook → `DRAFTKINGS-C-US-SB`

1. Proline / Direct / Canada / Ontario / Casino → `PROLINE-DIRECT-ON-CAS`

1. A second Deal with an identical Operator / Partner / Market / Vertical set produces -002; a third produces -003.

1. With -002 through -009 present, the tenth produces -010; with -099 present, the next produces -100.

1. Editing Operator, Partner, Market Country, Market State or Vertical on a Deal that already has an `External_Deal_ID__c` leaves the ID unchanged.

1. Clearing `External_Deal_ID__c` on an existing Deal and saving regenerates it.

1. A bulk insert of 200 Deals with distinct field sets populates all 200 IDs.

1. No Deal saves with NOOP, NOMKT or XXX in its ID when all five source fields are populated.

## Testing Notes

* **The "Get_Highest_Match may cause performance issues" warning on activation is expected — ignore it.** It is Salesforce's generic prompt to filter a same-object query down to the triggering record. Doing that would break the feature, since the element exists to find other Deals sharing the base key. Flow bulkifies Get Records, so a 200-record insert is one query.

* Before-save flows cannot read formula fields on the triggering record. `Market_State_Code__c` and `Market_Country_Code__c` are unavailable here, which is why fxStateCode inlines the mapping. Cross-object references such as `Operator__r.Operator_External_ID__c` do work.

* Verify a before-save flow satisfies the field-level Required flag on `External_Deal_ID__c`. If the save is rejected on the required check, uncheck Required at field level and rely on the flow.

* **Do not test by deleting Deals.** A deleted Deal keeps its unique index entry for 15 days in the Recycle Bin, but Get Records cannot see it — the query returns nothing, the flow generates the base key, and the save fails with DUPLICATE_VALUE against an invisible record. Set `Deal_Status__c` to Closed or Inactive instead, or purge the Recycle Bin between tests.

* Suffix padding must be consistent. An unpadded suffix such as -2 sorts above -002 in a descending text sort, so the flow would read -2 on every run, compute 3 every time, and fail on the second version.

* Sentinels are deliberate: NOOP = Operator Account missing its OP- external ID; NOMKT = no Market Country and no Market State; XXX = a Vertical value added to the picklist without updating the CASE; -OVERFLOW = more than 999 versions of one base key. Each fails visibly rather than producing a silent blank.

* Regression baseline: this logic regenerates all 120 migrated Deals that carry a Vertical byte-identically, including `HIGH5-GD-US-SC-002`. Source: Wagertech_Airtable_to_SF_Migration_Workbook_DRAFT_2026-07-24.xlsx, Deals tab.

## Out of Scope

* Any validation rule locking Operator / Partner / Market / Vertical once `External_Deal_ID__c` is set. Not required for this release.

* Backfill of existing Deals. The blank-only entry criteria covers any Deal whose ID is empty; migrated Deals already carry theirs.

* Publishing the ID to the CMS (covered by the CMS integration stories).

## Additional Notes

* The ID is generated once and never recalculated. If a user later corrects the Operator, Market or Vertical on a Deal, the ID keeps its original values and will no longer describe the record. This is accepted: the ID is an integration key, not a label. Name carries the readable description and is kept current by Deal - Before Save - Set Deal Name.

* The correction path for a Deal created with wrong information is a new Deal with the correct values. The original should be set to Closed or Inactive, not deleted.

* fxStateCode duplicates the mapping in `Market_State_Code__c`. Note this in the flow description so the two are kept in sync. The state list is static and the flow fires once per record, so a future divergence cannot retroactively alter an existing ID.

* Territory branches (PR, VI, GU, AS, MP) are carried in fxStateCode but are not values in the `Market_State__c` picklist. They are inert until added.

* The PT- prefixed partner value is the integration key only. The ID uses `Partner_Code__c` (GD, not PT-GD).

* The counter assumes no base key is a prefix of another base key. This holds because vertical abbreviations are a fixed closed set and state codes are two characters.

* Within a single bulk insert, two new Deals sharing the same base key will both generate the base key and the second will fail on the unique index. This is the correct outcome for duplicate natural keys in one load, but the error message will not explain it.

## Open Questions

* None.

## Source ref

Deal metadata review 2026-08-20. Format reverse-engineered from Wagertech_Airtable_to_SF_Migration_Workbook_DRAFT_2026-07-24.xlsx (Deals tab, 132 rows). External ID tokens from Wagertech_Operator_Partner_External_IDs_DRAFT_2026-08-13.xlsx.

comments.body:
RESCOPED: field exists but formula is defective — proof criterion tests a value the emoji formula never emits (max 10/11 achievable), and it references First Bet fields (being removed) + Sign_Up_Date_Old__c. Rewrite against Open Questions Q2 field set. Emily's 2026-07-28 19:44 doc comments may close the field-set blocker — verifying.

Formula-fix scope folded into this ticket (no separate ticket): replace proof criterion with the three \*_Proof_Attached_\_c checkboxes, remove First Bet + \_Old field references, align to Q2 field set, regression-test 100% achievable.

**UNBLOCKED — Open Questions Q2 confirmed complete by Emily Vandenberg, 2026-08-10.**

Sign Up Completion % is driven by exactly these components:

1. Sign Up is related to a **Player** and a **Deal** (Deal carries Operator, Partner, Vertical, Market)

1. **Sign Up Proof**, **Deposit Proof**, **Wager Proof** URLs are populated — presence only, we cannot validate legitimacy

1. **Affiliate Sign Up Date** and **Deposit Date** populated _(note: renaming to Sign Up Date / Registration Date per BUILD-58)_

1. **Deposit Amount** populated

1. **Referrer**, **Referrer Type**, **Payout Amount** populated _OR_ **No Referrer** = True

1. Sign Up is **not** Flagged for Fraud

**No Referrer behaviour** — Kobi's spec, doc thread 2026-07-24: "When Checked, we'll simply ignore empty values for referrer, referrer type and payout amounts when it comes to Sign up Completion % and any related automation." Emily: "that makes sense to me." Excluded from both numerator and denominator.

**Wager Proof was a late addition** — Lina added it 2026-07-28, Emily confirmed 2026-08-10. If the formula predates that, it is wrong.

**Remove auto-completion.** The Q2 line about auto-advancing to Completed at 100% is struck through in the doc and superseded by DECISION-04: completion is manual via the Complete button only. Delete any record-triggered automation flipping Status at 100%.

**⚠️ ONE OPEN ITEM — needs Emily:** First Wager Date was decided on the same day (Q12, BUILD-122) but is **not** in this criteria list. Confirm whether it counts toward Completion %. Do not assume either way.

Final Requirements from the Open Questions Document: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HUo7sC2robjOPn73g_km6VgAYfWVgkCx8FKiIl8nN1k/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.nt2k3z5a32l9](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HUo7sC2robjOPn73g_km6VgAYfWVgkCx8FKiIl8nN1k/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.nt2k3z5a32l9)

1. Sign Up Record is related to a Player & Deal (the related Deal record would hold the Operator, Partner, Vertical, Market information for the Sign Up Record. 
2. Sign Up Proof, Deposit Proof, Wager Proof url fields are filled in. (Note we cannot validate if the values in these fields are legitimate, but we can run validation to ensure there is a value for the fields. )
3. Affiliate Sign Up Date and Deposit Date are filled in.
4. Deposit Amount is filled in. 
5. Referrer, Referrer Type and Payout Amount are filled in or No Referrer is selected. 

1. When No Referrer = True, then Sign Up Completion % ignores Referrer, Referrer Type, Payout Amount

1. Sign Up record is not Flagged for Fraud.

## **What Changes vs. the Old Formula**

**Removed** (5 criteria dropped):

* `Operator__c` — now implicitly covered by `Deal__c` (Deal holds Operator, Partner, Market, Vertical)
* `Partner__c` — same reason
* `Market__c` — same reason
* `Deal_Rep_Assignment__c` — not in new requirements
* `Rep__c` — not in new requirements
* `Sign_Up_Date_Old__c` — replaced by `Affiliate_Signup_Date__c`
* `First_Bet_DateTime__c` — not in new requirements
* `First_Bet_Amount__c <> 0` — replaced by `Deposit_Amount__c`
* `Proof_Status__c = "Complete"` — replaced by 3 individual proof URL fields

**Added** (new criteria):

* `Sign_up_Proof__c` not blank
* `Deposit_Proof__c` not blank
* `Wager_Proof__c` not blank
* `Affiliate_Signup_Date__c` not blank
* `Deposit_Date__c` not blank
* `Deposit_Amount__c` not blank and ≠ 0
* Referrer block (see logic below)
* `NOT(Fraud_Flag__c)`

## **Key Design Decisions**

### **1. Referrer / No Referrer — Single Combined Criterion**

Rather than a dynamic denominator, the entire referrer section as **one combined criterion** that evaluates to `1` if either:

* `No_Referrer__c = TRUE` _(auto-satisfied, fields ignored)_, OR
* All three are filled: `Referrer__c`, `Referral_Type__c`, and `Payout_Amount__c` ≠ 0

[@Kobi Kunasekaran](https://app.asana.com/1/1202721605677544/profile/1203115293332591) please confirm if this is ok, the payout amount is populated by a flow.

[Update Payout Amount](https://nosoftware-nosoftware-7430--partialsb.sandbox.lightning.force.com/builder_platform_interaction/flowBuilder.app?flowId=301WJ00000xXwMfYAK)

### **2. Fraud Flag — One Criterion**

`NOT(Fraud_Flag__c)` scores 1 point when the record is clean, 0 when flagged. A fraudulent record is capped at 9/10 max.

### **3. Amount Checks (Deposit Amount, Payout Amount)**

Following the same pattern as the original `First_Bet_Amount__c` check — validating both not-blank **and** `<> 0` to avoid "filled with zero" false positives.

fields.description:
Objective

A returning player should land back in the existing Sign-Up queue, not create a duplicate record.

Implementation Requirements

* When a new Study Link Click arrives for an existing Archived Sign-Up, and the click occurs AFTER a defined grace period has elapsed since archival, reactivate the Sign-Up instead of creating a new one

* Grace period stored in a CUSTOM SETTING so admins can change it without editing automation. Set to 2 days for now

* Archived Sign-Up is defined as Status = Archived AND not flagged for fraud

* Fraud-flagged archived Sign-Ups are NEVER auto-reactivated

* On reactivation: Status -> In Progress; clear Archive Reason and Other Reason (Archived)

* Auto-reactivation applies ONLY when the click matches an existing Sign-Up on BOTH Player AND Deal. No match -> create a new Sign-Up as normal

Acceptance Criteria

* Click inside the grace period does not reactivate

* Click outside the grace period reactivates and clears archive reasons

* Fraud-flagged archived Sign-Ups are skipped

* Non-matching clicks still create new Sign-Ups

Dependencies / ARCHITECTURE NOTE

BUILD-04 (production Study Link Click resolution flow). This is a NEW BRANCH of that flow, not a standalone automation. Do NOT build a second record-triggered flow on Study Link Click — scope it into BUILD-04. See the pinned note on BUILD-04.

Estimate: M · \~10h (within BUILD-04)

Source: Wagertech Additional User Stories, July 2026 — item 41.

Objective

Drive record access and field state from Fraud Review Status.

Implementation Requirements

* Suspected / Under Review / Confirmed -> record read-only for Reps; Admins retain edit access

* Currently implemented via Lightning page display filters — confirm sufficient or harden

* Dismissed -> clear Fraud Flag, Fraud Review Status, Fraud Reason and Other Reason (Fraud)

* Dismissed -> return Sign-Up Status to its PREVIOUS Status, not to In Progress (records can be flagged after Completion)

Acceptance Criteria

* A Completed Sign-Up that is flagged then dismissed returns to Completed

* Reps cannot edit a record in Suspected/Under Review/Confirmed

* Dismissal leaves no residual fraud data on the record

Dependencies

* BUILD-35 (Previous Status field) — HARD dependency

* DECISION-02 (Fraud Flag impact on Player Status) — BLOCKING, unanswered

RISK / CONTROL GAP

Lightning page display filters HIDE fields; they do not prevent edits via API, list view inline edit, or flows. If the Rep lock needs to be a real control, this requires validation rules or field-level security. Raise with Ops before sign-off.

Estimate: M · \~8h

Source: Wagertech Additional User Stories, July 2026 — items 9.3 and 45 (merged; both specify the same Dismissed behaviour).
fields.summary: BUILD-34 — Fraud Review Status automations: record lock and Dismissed clear-down

comments.body: CONFLICT TO CONFIRM (2026-07-30, from feedback tracker row 41): client's written workflow says Dismissed → 'returns to In Progress and unlocks'. Current design (with BUILD-35) restores PREVIOUS status — which for a flagged-after-completion record means back to Completed, not In Progress. Confirm with Ops which behavior wins (recommend: restore previous status; 'In Progress' in their text likely assumed the common case). Also note row 41 confirms lock-on-Suspected — real enforcement needs validation rules, not just page filters (existing risk note).

**UNBLOCKED — Open Questions Q7 resolved.**

Decision: "Dismissed Fraud Review should return the record back to the **previous status** before it was flagged."

Agreed by Lina Ceniccola, 2026-08-03: "previous works!" (Emily proposed; Joyce was asked but never replied in-thread.)

**This overrides** the earlier feedback-notes behaviour of "returns the record to In Progress". If a flow currently hardcodes `In Progress`, that is the change. A Completed Sign Up that gets flagged and then dismissed goes back to **Completed**, not In Progress.

Build:

* Stamp `Previous_Status__c` at the moment of flagging (field is BUILD-35, already Ready for Review; make it read-only for all users per BUILD-113).

* Record-triggered flow on Fraud Review Status = `Dismissed` → Status = Previous Status, then clear the stash.

* Dismissal must also **release the record lock** — locking is part of this card's scope.

**Related open item:** DECISION-06 asks whether a _Completed_ record locks too. If it does, this dismissal path needs to restore the right lock state, not just the right status. Sequence DECISION-06 before finalising the flow.

Update: When Fraud Review Status is set to Dismissed, reset Flag status on the Sign Up record, i.e Uncheck Fraud checkbox, clear Fraud Review Status and Fraud Reason. 

Fraud satus fields should be tracking field history for future review.

Source: Kobi, 2026-08-11. Supports BUILD-118 (Market display field).

=== OBJECTIVE ===

Add two read-only formula fields on Deal__c that derive short codes from the existing Market Country / Market State picklists (which hold full names). These are the reusable building blocks for the Market display field, list views, reporting groupings and any outbound CMS payload that needs a code rather than a full name.

Reps continue to maintain Market_Country\__c and Market_State_\_c only. Neither new field is editable.

=== WHY FORMULA, NOT A MAPPING TABLE ===

Custom Metadata Types were evaluated and rejected: formula fields can only reference $CustomMetadata with a STATIC record name, so there is no dynamic lookup from a field value. A CMT approach would require Flow or Apex, which is over-engineered for a display/derivation string. Hardcoded CASE is the correct pattern here.

Note for future reference: renaming the picklist API values to codes (label stays the full name) would remove the need for the state CASE entirely, since TEXT() returns the API value. Rejected for now because the CMS integration and data migration mappings write the full names, and changing API values pre-go-live would ripple into those. Revisit if the codes are ever needed in more places.

=== FIELD 1: Market Country Code ===

API Name: Market_Country_Code__c

Label: Market Country Code

Type: Formula (Text)

Blank handling: Treat blank fields as Blanks

Help text: Auto-derived from Market Country. US, CA, or 'US & CA'.

Requirements:

* Market Country = United States -> US

* Market Country = Canada -> CA

* Market Country = United States & Canada -> US & CA

* Market Country = blank -> blank

Formula:

CASE(TEXT(Market_Country__c),

"United States", "US",

"Canada", "CA",

"United States & Canada", "US & CA",

"")

=== FIELD 2: Market State Code ===

API Name: Market_State_Code__c

Label: Market State Code

Type: Formula (Text)

Blank handling: Treat blank fields as Blanks

Help text: Auto-derived from Market State. Shows 'Multi-state' when no single state is selected.

Requirements:

* Market State has a value -> 2-letter USPS / Canada Post subdivision code

* Market State blank AND Market Country has a value -> "Multi-state"

* Market State blank AND Market Country blank -> blank

Coverage is intentionally the FULL US + Canada set (69 branches), not only the values currently in the picklist value set:

* 50 US states + District of Columbia = 51

* US territories (PR, VI, GU, AS, MP) = 5 (dormant until added to the picklist)

* Canada: 10 provinces + 3 territories = 13

This means no formula edit is needed when a market opens up.

Formula size: 1,584 of 3,900 characters.

Formula:

IF(ISPICKVAL(Market_State__c, ""),

IF(ISPICKVAL(Market_Country__c, ""), "", "Multi-state"),

CASE(TEXT(Market_State__c),

/\* US states + DC (51) \*/

=== EXPECTED RESULTS ===

Canada | Ontario | CA | ON

United States | Ohio | US | OH

Canada | (blank) | CA | Multi-state

United States & Canada | (blank) | US & CA | Multi-state

(blank) | (blank) | (blank) | (blank)

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

1\. Both fields exist on Deal__c as Formula (Text), blank handling = Blanks, and pass Check Syntax.

2\. Every value currently in the Market_State__c value set returns a non-blank 2-letter code (no value falls through to the empty else branch).

3\. Market Country set with Market State blank returns "Multi-state" on the state code field.

4\. Both fields blank when Market Country is blank.

5\. FLS: readable = true on WT_Deal_Read and WT_Deal_Edit. Both fields are formula (read-only), so no editable permission is granted anywhere.

6\. Fields added to the Deal layout / Deal record page per BUILD-120, and available for report and list view grouping.

=== NOTES / RISKS ===

* "US & CA" contains a space-ampersand-space. Fine for display, but it is a delimiter risk if this field is ever consumed by an outbound CMS payload, BI grouping or the Airtable import. If the value leaves Salesforce, consider US+CA or US/CA instead.

* Market_State_Code__c returns "Multi-state" rather than a 2-character code. Intentional and useful for report grouping, but it means the field is not a clean 2-char code column for integrations expecting strict codes.

* Edge case not yet decided: Market Country = United States & Canada WITH a single state selected. The dependent picklist allows this (every state lists United States & Canada as a controlling value), and the codes would read e.g. ON / US & CA. Confirm with Joyce whether that combination is real before hardening it.

* Dependency direction: BUILD-118 (Market display field) consumes both of these fields and should not be built first.

=== METADATA LOCATION ===

force-app/main/default/objects/Deal\__c/fields/Market_State_Code_\_c.field-meta.xml

Source: Kobi, 2026-08-11. Depends on BUILD-124 (Market_Country_Code\__c / Market_State_Code_\_c). Revises the Deal Name format set in BUILD-117.

=== OBJECTIVE ===

Rebuild the two Deal label formulas to read Operator - Market - Vertical using the new market short-code fields, and collapse separators when a segment is blank.

Two changes from the previous format:

1\. Partner is REMOVED from the label (intentional - see Decisions below).

2\. Market is rendered from the short-code fields (ON · CA) instead of the full picklist names (Canada Ontario).

=== DEFECT BEING FIXED ===

Both original formulas referenced Partner__r.Name and the market picklists WITHOUT blank guards. Any Deal with no Partner rendered a double separator and an orphaned space, e.g.:

Bet99 - - Canada Ontario - Casino

The new formulas guard every optional segment.

=== FIELD 1: Deal_Name__c (Formula, Text) ===

Original:

Operator__r.Name

& IF(ISBLANK(Partner__c), "",

" - " & Partner__r.Name)

& IF(TEXT(Market_Country__c) = "", "",

" - " & TEXT(Market_Country__c) &

IF(TEXT(Market_State\__c) = "", "", " " & TEXT(Market_State_\_c)))

& IF(TEXT(Vertical__c) = "", "",

" - " & TEXT(Vertical__c))

New:

Operator__r.Name

& IF(ISBLANK(Market_Country_Code__c), "",

" - " & IF(Market_State_Code__c = "Multi-state",

Market_Country_Code__c & " · Multi-state",

Market_State_Code\__c & " · " & Market_Country_Code_\_c))

& IF(ISPICKVAL(Vertical\__c, ""), "", " - " & TEXT(Vertical_\_c))

=== FIELD 2: Deal__c (Formula, Text - hyperlink) ===

Original:

HYPERLINK( "/" & Id, Operator\__r.Name & " - " & Partnerr.Name & " - " & TEXT(Market_Countryc) & " " & TEXT(Market_Statec) & " - " & TEXT(Vertical_\_c), "\_self" )

New:

HYPERLINK("/" & Id, Deal_Name__c, "\_self")

This references Deal_Name__c rather than duplicating the logic, so the plain-text label and the hyperlink label can never drift. Confirmed to compile.

=== EXPECTED OUTPUT ===

Operator | Market Country | Market State | Vertical | Deal Name

Bet99 | Canada | Ontario | Casino | Bet99 - ON · CA - Casino

Bet99 | United States | Ohio | Sports | Bet99 - OH · US - Sports

Bet99 | United States | (blank) | Sports | Bet99 - US · Multi-state - Sports

Bet99 | (blank) | (blank) | Casino | Bet99 - Casino

=== COMPILED-SIZE CONSTRAINT (important for anyone editing these) ===

The first attempt had Deal_Name\__c reference Market_Displayc, which in turn references Market_State_Code_\_c (a 69-branch CASE). Salesforce inlines referenced formula fields into one compiled expression, and this failed:

"Compiled formula is too big to execute (20,367 characters). Maximum size is 15,000 characters."

Resolved by having Deal_Name\__c reference Market_State_Codec / Market_Country_Code_\_c DIRECTLY and drop the flag emoji, which removed a nesting layer and brought it under 15,000.

Consequence: there is limited headroom left. Do NOT add further nested formula references to Deal_Name\__c or Dealc without re-running Check Syntax. If more headroom is ever needed, the fix is to sever the chain - either convert Market_State_Code_\_c to a Text field populated by a before-save Flow, or rename the Market State picklist API values to the 2-letter codes so the 69-branch CASE disappears entirely.

=== DECISIONS ===

* Partner removed from the Deal label. Deliberate. Note the side effect: partner deals and Direct deals are no longer distinguishable by name alone, so reporting and list views must surface Partner as its own column. If this needs reversing, insert after Operator__r.Name:

& IF(ISBLANK(Partner\__c), "", " - " & Partner_\_r.Name)

* Flag emoji excluded from both label fields. The emoji lives only in the UI display field (BUILD-118). Keeps Deal Name clean for CSV export, email templates and any outbound CMS payload, and avoids the Windows no-flag-font rendering issue.

* Separator is a middle dot ( · ) inside the market segment and a hyphen ( - ) between segments, so the market reads as one unit.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

1\. Both formulas pass Check Syntax and report compiled size under 15,000 characters.

2\. A Deal with no Partner renders no double separator and no orphaned space.

3\. A Deal with Market Country set and Market State blank renders "US · Multi-state".

4\. A Deal with Market Country blank renders Operator - Vertical only.

5\. Deal\__c hyperlink navigates to the Deal record in the same tab and its label text matches Deal_Name_\_c exactly.

6\. Deal list views (BUILD-119) and the Deal record page (BUILD-120) reflect the new label.

=== OPEN QUESTION ===

Deal_Name\__c and Deal_\_c now render identical strings - one as plain text, one as a hyperlink. Two adjacent columns showing the same text will read as a duplicate to reps. Decide before BUILD-119/BUILD-120 lock the layouts whether to keep both (HYPERLINK fields export as raw HTML and do not sort cleanly, which is the usual reason to keep a plain-text twin) or retire one.

=== METADATA LOCATION ===

force-app/main/default/objects/Deal\__c/fields/Deal_Name_\_c.field-meta.xml

force-app/main/default/objects/Deal\__c/fields/Deal_\_c.field-meta.xml

fields.description:
Before-save flow that stamps Benchmark Last Reviewed whenever Tracking Benchmark is edited.

=== IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS ===

* Record-triggered before-save (fast field update) flow on Account. Entry: record is updated AND Tracking Benchmark IsChanged -> set the date.

* Kobi reviewed it live and approved: 'Tracking benchmark is changed. Every time a record is updated and tracking benchmark is changed. We're going to set the date. Yeah, this is fine. This look good.'

* NAMING CONVENTION: \[Account\] Before Save – Set Benchmark Last Reviewed. Per Kobi: 'we label it so that it has the object, whether it's a before save flow after save flow, and then the description.' Fast field updates are before-save; actions and related records are after-save. Screen flows get 'Screen' in front.

* Field must stay manually editable despite being auto-set.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

* Editing Tracking Benchmark updates the date; editing any other field does not.

=== NOTES ===

* ALREADY BUILT. Taryn built it before the Aug 17 call and Kobi approved it live. It is the only flow she has built so far — 'No, that was the only one I created.' Add the actual flow API name to the card.

* Accepted limitation, confirmed with Joyce on Aug 13: if the benchmark is reviewed and the value doesn't change, the date goes stale unless someone edits it manually. Joyce: 'That's fine.'

* The requirement flipped: Taryn relayed that the client wanted it automated; Kobi had it as manual — 'Automated. Okay... I don't remember.' Resolved in the client's favour.

=== SOURCE ===

* Aug 13 call — Joyce confirmed auto-stamp

* Slack Taryn Aug 14 — built

* Aug 17 call — reviewed and approved live

Dependencies: BUILD-127

Owner (proposed): Taryn Reithofer

Remember to update the requirements documentation as part of this change.

# DL-6: Link Validation Logic

_Confirm how Assignment Cap enforcement is split between Salesforce and the CMS, so no redundant validation gets built._

* Assignment Cap enforcement happens on the CMS side, not Salesforce

### IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

* No Salesforce-side validation logic needs to be built for this story. Salesforce passes Assignment Cap and Active to the CMS; the CMS enforces the cap at the point of link assignment.

* Provenance: DL-6 (Deal Record User Stories doc).
* Scope here is confirming/documenting the SF → CMS field hand-off, not building enforcement logic in Salesforce.

fields.summary: BUILD-63 — Deal Links child object

comments.body:
Added some fields based on this mock up

[https://deal-management.netlify.app/deal-record.html](https://deal-management.netlify.app/deal-record.html)
[Test Data](https://nosoftware-nosoftware-7430--partialsb.sandbox.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Links__c/a0FWJ000004k91B2AQ/view?ws=%2Flightning%2Fr%2FDeal__c%2Fa00WJ00000XjC76YAF%2Fview)

**⚠️ Review risk: this was built against a link↔rep cardinality that is still contradictory across three calls.**

* **Jul 28, Joyce:** all links sit at deal level, CMS picks from a dropdown — implicitly **one-to-many**.

* **Aug 4, Emily \[14:45\]:** "Typically like a rep for a deal wouldn't have more than one link… it would be managed on Salesforce" — then \[16:12\]: "they can, in their lifetime, have, like, one-to-one. there's a potential for them to switch to a different link on the same deal."

* **Aug 4, Joyce \[15:43\]:** "I think what you're saying is, like, we just do one-to-one" — after acknowledging she changed the mock-up at the offsite without discussion.

* But Emily also confirmed there **will** be rep sharing / multiple reps on one link — which contradicts one-to-one.

The attached Deal mockup shows a Links related list with a **Reps count column** (4, 2, 0) and a **Default** flag — i.e. many reps per link, with one default. That is a third model again.

**Before accepting this review, pin down:** (a) can one link serve multiple reps simultaneously? (b) can one rep hold multiple active links on the same deal? (c) what does the Default flag actually govern?

Also noted Jul 28: there is **no Salesforce-side guardrail** that a link belongs to only one rep — that has to be enforced in the CMS. If (a) is "no", we are relying on a system we do not control to protect our data model. Worth pushing back on.
Closing this as having been built. Will create addtiional tickets to update the fields and naming conventions as the CMS <> SF Integration details are solidified.

fields.description:
Objective

Auto-calculate the referral payout on a Sign-Up from the signup market and referral currency.

Implementation Requirements

* Populate Payout Amount automatically when Referrer is populated AND Referral Type is Cash or Bet

* Recalculate whenever Referral Type changes

* Core rules:

* Payout currency = Referral Currency

* Payout amount determined by Signup Currency (market-based)

* Payout matrix:

* CAD signup + CAD referral -> 25 CAD cash / 40 CAD bet credit

* CAD signup + USD referral -> 20 USD cash / 30 USD bet credit

* USD signup + CAD referral -> 50 CAD cash / 80 CAD bet credit

* USD signup + USD referral -> 30 USD cash / 50 USD bet credit

* USD amounts for CAD signups are FIXED (20 / 30) — no FX calculation anywhere

Acceptance Criteria

* All four matrix combinations produce the correct amount and currency

* Changing Referral Type recalculates

* No FX conversion is performed anywhere in this logic

Dependencies

BUILD-15 (field — complete).

Open Questions

The 2026-07-20 Deal Rep Assignment architecture decision appears to answer this: Salesforce replaces Airtable as the system of record for rep assignment, with one active state per Deal and the Deal / Deal Rep Assignment split. fields.description:
## Objective

Create two global picklist value sets used by Deal, Operator, and future objects. Market and Vertical are picklists in Phase 1 (not custom objects).

## Implementation Requirements

* Create global value set WT_Market with starting values (verbatim from the current rates data): ON; ON-CAN; ROC; USA; NJ-USA; PA-USA; MI-USA; IL-USA; OH-USA; KS-USA; NC-USA; NY-USA; MI/NJ-USA; OH/KS-USA; NC/MA-USA; Sweeps
* Create global value set WT_Vertical with values: Sportsbook; Casino; DFS; Sweepstakes; Social Casino
* Both sets restricted (no free-text entries)

## Acceptance Criteria

* Both global value sets exist with the values above and are available to reference from custom fields

## Testing Notes

Reference each set from a scratch field, then delete the scratch field.

## Out of Scope

Market custom object (kept as a documented graduation path if reporting later needs state-level rollups).

## Open Questions

* ON and ON-CAN both appear in the source data — same market? Merge before go-live if so.
* 'Sweeps' appears as a geography value in the rates file but looks like a vertical — client to confirm what it denotes.
* Link tracker data adds WV, AZ, CO and Canada-wide variants (CA, Canada excl. Ontario) — add these values now or as needed?
* Add Poker to WT_Vertical? One Poker deal exists in the data. And does Fantasy map to DFS?

## Additional Notes

* Value API names match the source data exactly so the data load (POC-11) needs no mapping step.
* Composite values (MI/NJ-USA, OH/KS-USA) cannot roll up to state level in reports — accepted trade-off for Phase 1.

---

fields.description:
**Type:** Spike / Investigation (timeboxed) · **Epic:** Foundation & Sign-Ups (Phase 1) — Proof / Logging · **Related decision:** D-File-Storage (Salesforce Files vs. external links)

**User story**

As the Wagertech operations team, we want proof-of-deposit images and videos to be uploaded and viewed from within the signup/player record in Salesforce — and stored on a platform that keeps them linked to those records without driving up Salesforce file-storage costs — so that we can retire the manual Dropbox + Excel process and have a single, auditable system of record for deposit proof.

**Context**

Today deposit proof is uploaded to Dropbox and tracked in Excel, with no reliable link back to the signup or player. Target is in-Salesforce upload and retrieval, with the actual binary files held in lower-cost storage. This is an investigation, not a build — the output is a recommended approach plus rough cost/effort to implement it.

**Investigation questions**

* Realistic volume/size: files per signup, image vs. video mix, average/max size, monthly growth, retention period.
* Viable storage approaches and how they compare: (a) Salesforce Files/ContentVersion (native); (b) Salesforce Files Connect to an external store (SharePoint/Google Drive); (c) external blob store (e.g. AWS S3) with linked references surfaced via LWC/Files Connect; (d) keep current cloud store (Dropbox) but integrate uploads + linking via API.
* For each: how upload-from-within-Salesforce works for an end user, how the file links to the Player/Signup record, what retrieval/preview looks like, and where the cost lands (Salesforce storage vs. external).
* Compliance/PII: regulated-gambling deposit proof likely contains sensitive data — access control, encryption, retention, audit requirements; which options satisfy them. (Flag to compliance owner.)
* Migration: can existing Dropbox files be back-linked to records, or go-forward only?

**Evaluation criteria**

End-user upload/view experience · linkage integrity to Player/Signup · Salesforce storage cost impact · external storage + integration cost · implementation effort/complexity · security/compliance fit · migration feasibility · maintainability.

**Out of scope**

Building the integration; migrating historical files — these become follow-on stories once a direction is chosen.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Volume/size assumptions documented (with source — confirmed with ops or estimated).
2. At least 3 storage options compared in a short matrix against the criteria above.
3. Clear recommended option with rationale, rough implementation effort/hours, and ongoing cost implication.
4. Open compliance/security questions captured and routed to the compliance owner.
5. Follow-on build stories identified for the chosen path.
6. Findings reviewed with Joyce/Emily and logged against the D-File-Storage decision.

**Timebox:** 2-3 hours, check-in with Kobi if more than 2-3 hours are needed.
fields.summary: SPIKE — Evaluate storage options for proof-of-deposit media (images/videos)

PARKED — additive to the baseline custom file properties; we would apply both.

Why it exists: custom file properties are readable via the API but are NOT VISIBLE OR FILTERABLE IN THE DRIVE WEB INTERFACE. Drive Labels are the upgrade that lets analysts and auditors filter and search proofs inside Drive itself. A genuine usability gain for anyone reviewing proofs in bulk.

Depends entirely on the WagerTech side:

* Google Workspace Business Standard or above — Labels are NOT available on lower editions

* A Workspace admin to define the label taxonomy in the Google Admin console. LABELS CANNOT BE CREATED BY AN INTEGRATION; they are admin-configured structure. Needs a short session with their admin to set fields matching our metadata table

* Ceiling of roughly ten labels per file, which our set fits comfortably

Not needed for the POC and NOT needed for automation — automation reads the custom properties. Worth it only if humans will browse and filter the library in Drive.

Effort: \~3h on our side plus the admin session.

Source: Drive Storage doc §3.2, D5.

fields.description:
PARKED — fully additive. Nothing in the base build needs to change to accommodate it later.

What the base build gives you: each deal carries its current sync status and the message from its most recent attempt. Salesforce field history will show THAT a deal moved in and out of Failed, but for LONG TEXT FIELDS IT DOES NOT RETAIN PREVIOUS VALUES. If a deal fails Monday with one error and again Thursday with a different one, Thursday overwrites Monday.

Day to day that is fine — Ops needs to know what is broken now. It matters only for cross-time questions: which errors are most common, whether a particular operator's deals fail repeatedly, whether the failure rate changed after a CMS release, how long failures take to clear.

Proposed solution:

* A dedicated integration error log object, DELIBERATELY GENERIC rather than deal-specific, so it serves any Salesforce object pushing to any external system

* One record per attempt: source object and record, target system, direction, event type, outcome, HTTP status, request and response detail, timestamp, retry count

* Retention policy so data does not accumulate indefinitely

* A standard set of reports

Effort 12-20h INDICATIVE ONLY — not scoped in detail; would be scoped as separate work. Grows in value as SF-CMS touchpoints increase beyond deal publishing.

Source: CMS Integration Design v1, §4.5, D10.

  3. Payment Terms

fields.description:
## Outcome

An Operator record shows every partner it does business with, and its own direct billing terms, without anyone reading the Deal list to work it out. A Partner record shows the same from its side.

Today both answers are inferred from Deals and the inference is unreliable. The associated-partner count is derived from a semicolon-separated string of partner record Ids in a 255-character text field, so it stops being correct at about thirteen partners, and it counts partners whose deals closed. Direct billing terms sit in an Operator-level section controlled by a single Direct-or-Via-Partner picklist, which cannot express an operator that has both a direct deal and deals through an affiliate network at the same time — the situation WagerTech raised on 2026-08-28.

## Scope

A relationship record between an Operator and a Partner, created the first time a Deal joins them and deactivated when their last active Deal goes away. Direct billing terms held on the relationship row for the shared Direct partner record. Retirement of the Operator-level billing section and the Billing Relationship picklist. Partner and operator counts rebuilt as counts of relationship rows.

## Success measures

* Partner and operator counts stay correct past thirteen relationships and exclude ended ones.
* An Operator with a direct arrangement and two affiliate partners shows both facts on its record, each linking to the relevant record.
* No billing value exists in two places.

## Children

* Confirm whether an Operator can hold more than one set of direct billing terms
* Operator–Partner Relationship records created and deactivated from Deals
* Hold direct billing terms on the Direct relationship record
* Move Operator billing values onto Direct relationship rows and retire the Operator billing section
* Show direct billing on the Operator record without leaving it
* Rebuild the associated partner and operator counts from relationship records

## Background

Requirement source: _Operator & Partner Record Pages_ (Google Doc, 2026-08-28), section "Billing Relationship — needs rework". Design agreed with Kobi on 2026-09-14; it supersedes the 2026-08-17 position that the Deal itself was the junction between Operator and Partner, and absorbs the on-hold work to surface partner and operator information from Deal.

All direct deals attach to a single shared Partner Account named Direct (Partner External ID `PT-DIRECT`), which is why an operator's direct billing terms can live on its relationship row with that record rather than on the Operator itself.

fields.description:
## Outcome and context

Every direct deal attaches to the single shared Partner record named "Direct", so each Operator will have exactly one relationship row with it — and that row is where direct billing terms are going to live. That works if an Operator's direct terms are the same everywhere.

If terms can differ by market — a different billing entity, invoicing currency or payment terms for Ontario than for Alberta — then one row per Operator is the wrong shape. The relationship record would need a Market field, and its uniqueness key would need to include the market. Deals already carry a market, so the requirement is expressible; nothing stores billing terms against one today.

Changing this after rows exist and terms have been entered means a data migration, so it is worth ten minutes now.

## The question to answer

_Can WagerTech's direct billing terms with an operator differ by market — for example a different billing entity, invoicing currency, payment terms or tax ID for Ontario than for Alberta? If yes, which of those fields can vary?_

## Done when

* The answer is recorded on this ticket with who gave it and when.
* If yes: the list of fields that can vary is recorded, and _Operator–Partner Relationship records created and deactivated from Deals_ is updated to include a Market field and a market-aware uniqueness key before it is built.
* If no: the ticket records that one direct arrangement per Operator is confirmed.

## Dependencies

Blocks _Operator–Partner Relationship records created and deactivated from Deals_ (uniqueness key) and _Hold direct billing terms on the Direct relationship record_ (cardinality).

fields.description:
Outcome and context

Nothing in the org records that an Operator and a Partner work together. It is inferred from Deals every time it is needed, and the inference is a concatenated string of partner Ids in a 255-character field that stops being correct at about thirteen partners.

A record per Operator/Partner pair — created the first time a Deal joins them, deactivated when their last active Deal goes away — gives that fact a home that can be counted, filtered, reported on and given its own fields. Rows are never deleted, so a relationship that goes quiet keeps its history and anything a person typed on it, and comes back to life if a new deal starts.

Current state

  • No junction object exists.

  • Deal__c.Operator__c is a required lookup; Deal__c.Partner__c is optional but populated on all 28 Deals. Both are filtered to the matching Account record type and to Active status.

  • Deal__c.Deal_Status__c values are Active, Paused, Closed, Inactive, Review Required. The existing DLRS active-deal rollups treat only Active as active.

  • Lookup rollups in this org are done with DLRS — out-of-the-box rollups need master-detail.

Proposed solution

Object

  1. New object Operator Partner Relationship (Operator_Partner_Relationship__c). Auto-number Name, format OPR-{00000}. Org-wide default to match Deal__c. Tab, New action and a Lightning record page — rows are created by automation but people must be able to create and open them by hand.

  2. Fields:

    • Operator — Lookup(Account), required, filter RecordType = Operator.

    • Partner — Lookup(Account), required, filter RecordType = Partner. Deliberately not filtered on Active status, unlike the Deal lookups: a relationship has to survive its partner being deactivated.

    • Relationship Key — Text(80), Unique, case-insensitive, External ID. Set by automation as <Operator Id>-<Partner Id>. Record Ids rather than business codes, because the key's only job is enforcing one row per pair and Ids are immune to renames. If direct billing terms turn out to differ by market, the market value is appended to the key.

    • Status — Picklist, restricted, values Active / Inactive, default Active. Maintained by automation.

    • Is Direct — Formula (Checkbox): Partner__r.Partner_External_ID__c = "PT-DIRECT". Keyed on the external ID, not the Account Name and not Partner_Code__c: the external ID is already unique and case-insensitive, and WAGR-100 freezes it once set, so a rename cannot break this.

    • Active Deals — Number(18,0), DLRS target.

  3. New Relationship lookup on Deal__c to this object, set by the automation below. This is what makes the deal count a standard DLRS rollup instead of a hand-rolled counter, and it gives the relationship record a real Deals related list. (If there is a better way to count, say so on this ticket before building — the alternative is a flow that queries Deals on every change, which is the part that historically drifts.)

Automation 1 — Account_Deal_After_Save_Maintain_Relationship

  • Object / timing: Deal__c, after save, create and update.

  • Entry criteria: ISNEW() OR ISCHANGED(Operator__c) OR ISCHANGED(Partner__c) OR ISBLANK(Relationship__c) — and Partner__c is not blank.

  • Path: Run Asynchronously. See the note below — this is a deliberate choice, not a default.

  • Steps: 1. Build the key as Operator__c & "-" & Partner__c. 2. Get Records on Operator_Partner_Relationship__c where Relationship_Key__c equals it. 3. Found → if Status__c = 'Inactive' leave it alone, Automation 2 owns Status. Not found → Create Records with Operator, Partner, Relationship Key, Status Active. 4. Update Records on the triggering Deal setting Relationship__c.

  • Race handling: Two Deals for the same new pair saved at the same time both find nothing and both create. The unique key means the second create fails with DUPLICATE_VALUE. Put a fault connector on the Create that re-runs the Get and uses the row that won. This is the same guard as the SLC duplicate-Player fix — do not skip it because the window looks small.

  • Bulk: No DML inside a loop. One Get, one Create, one Update, each over a collection. Must survive a 200-record Deal load in one transaction and a 10,000-record data load in batches.

  • Recursion: The step 4 update re-fires the flow. On the second pass Relationship__c is populated and neither lookup changed, so entry criteria are false and it stops. Verify this rather than assume it.

  • Must not: Change any field on the relationship row other than the three it sets at creation. Never delete a row. Never write to a row's billing fields.

Why asynchronous. An after-save flow that errors rolls back the whole transaction, so a failure to write a bookkeeping row would block a user from saving a Deal — with a flow error, not a message they can act on. The relationship row is derived data; it is not worth failing a Deal for. Async means the row appears a moment later and a failure shows up in the weekly check instead of in a rep's face. The cost is that the Deal's Relationship lookup is briefly blank, which nothing reads synchronously.

Automation 2 — Account_OPR_Before_Save_Set_Status

  • Object / timing: Operator_Partner_Relationship__c, before save, create and update.

  • Entry criteria: ISNEW() OR ISCHANGED(Active_Deals__c).

  • Steps: Active_Deals__c = 0 → Status__c = 'Inactive'. Active_Deals__c > 0 → Status__c = 'Active'. Nothing else.

  • Why before-save: It is a same-record derivation, so before-save costs no extra DML and cannot recurse. DLRS updates the record with DML, which fires before-save flows normally. Note Active_Deals__c is a DLRS-populated Number, not a formula — a before-save flow could not read it if it were a formula, which is the trap this org has already hit once on the Deal dedupe key.

  • Must not: Touch billing fields, Operator, Partner or Relationship Key. A person editing billing values must not see Status move as a side effect.

Automation 3 — DLRS rule OPR_Active_Deal_Count

Count of Deal__c.Id where Deal_Status__c = 'Active', relationship field Relationship__c, parent Operator_Partner_Relationship__c, result field Active_Deals__c, Realtime. Same shape as the existing Deals_Operator_Active_Count. Realtime because Status has to follow the deal immediately; a scheduled rollup would leave the roster wrong for a day.

Automation 4 — Account_Deal_Scheduled_Report_Missing_Relationship

  • Object / timing: Scheduled-triggered flow on Deal__c, weekly, Sunday 02:00 America/Toronto.

  • Filter: Partner__c != null AND Relationship__c = null.

  • Steps: Collect the Deals, email Kobi one message listing them with links. Create nothing. Delete nothing. Change nothing.

  • Why report and not repair: Silent self-repair hides the cause. Every one of these is either an async failure or a load run with automation off, and both are worth knowing about.

  • The reverse case: Rows with no Deals — created by hand, or orphaned by a merge — are caught by a saved report (Active Deals = 0 AND Status = Active), not by this flow. Cheaper than a second scheduled job.

Field descriptions and help text

Operator — Description: The Operator Account in this relationship. Set by automation from the first Deal that links this Operator and Partner. Help Text: The operator side of this relationship.

Partner — Description: The Partner Account in this relationship. The shared Direct partner represents an operator's direct arrangement with WagerTech. Set by automation from the first Deal. Help Text: The partner side of this relationship. Direct means the operator deals with WagerTech directly.

Relationship Key — Description: Unique key enforcing one relationship record per Operator and Partner pair, built by automation as Operator Id followed by Partner Id. Do not edit. Editing or clearing it lets a duplicate relationship be created. Help Text: n/a — not on page layouts.

Status — Description: Active while the pair has at least one Active Deal, Inactive when it has none. Maintained by automation from the Active Deals count — do not set it by hand, the next deal change overwrites it. Inactive rows are kept, not deleted, so the relationship and anything recorded on it survives and returns to Active if a new deal starts. Inactive means there are no active deals right now, not that the relationship has ended. Help Text: Set automatically from the number of active deals.

Is Direct — Description: True when the Partner is the shared Direct record, identified by Partner External ID PT-DIRECT. Used to show the direct billing section and to exclude the Direct record from an operator's partner count. Help Text: n/a — not on page layouts.

Active Deals — Description: Number of Deals for this Operator and Partner pair with Deal Status Active. Maintained by DLRS. Drives the Status field. Help Text: Number of currently active deals between this operator and partner.

Deal.Relationship — Description: The Operator Partner Relationship this Deal belongs to, set by automation from the Deal's Operator and Partner. Do not edit — the automation resets it. Help Text: Set automatically. Change the Deal's Operator or Partner to move it.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Saving the first Deal between an Operator and a Partner creates one relationship row with Status Active; saving a second Deal between the same pair creates no additional row.

  2. Loading 200 Deals for the same new pair in a single operation creates exactly one row, and two Deals for the same new pair saved concurrently also produce exactly one — the second create hits the unique key and recovers onto the row that won.

  3. Changing a Deal's Partner attaches it to the correct relationship row, leaves the previous row in place, and moves the deal count off it.

  4. When the last Active Deal for a pair moves to any other status or is deleted, the row's Status becomes Inactive and the row still exists.

  5. A Deal on a previously Inactive pair becoming Active returns that row to Active without creating a second one.

  6. A relationship row created by hand for a pair with no Deals is neither modified nor removed by the automation or the weekly check.

  7. Values typed into fields on a relationship row are unchanged after any of the above, and editing one of those values does not move Status.

  8. A relationship row that fails to be created appears in the weekly email and does not block the Deal from saving.

What stays manual

Part of accepting this design, and the content of the operating note under Output:

  • A relationship that exists before any Deal — a partner in negotiation, or an operator whose direct billing terms need entering ahead of the first direct deal — is created by hand. The automation only ever reacts to a Deal.

  • The direct billing values themselves. Nothing derives a billing entity, tax ID or payment terms.

  • Deleting a row created in error. The automation never deletes; an admin does, after checking no Deal points at it.

  • Triaging whatever the weekly email reports. It reports; a person decides whether to re-save the Deal, create the row by hand, or investigate.

  • A bulk Deal load run with automation switched off leaves rows unmade in bulk. Someone re-saves the affected Deals afterwards.

  • Merging two Partner or Operator Accounts. Merge repoints the losing Account's child records to the winner. If the winner already has a row for the same counterparty, the unique key blocks the merge until a person deactivates or deletes the redundant row. Verify this during the build — it decides whether merges need a documented pre-step.

  • Judging whether a quiet relationship has actually ended. Status only knows the deal count. If the team needs "ended" as a distinct fact, that is a human-set field the automation must never overwrite — confirm before building, it is cheap now and awkward to retrofit.

Out of scope

Billing fields on the relationship record, and replacing the associated-partner and associated-operator counts. Both are separate tickets.

Dependencies

Depends on Confirm whether an Operator can hold more than one set of direct billing terms — it decides the shape of the uniqueness key.

Relates to WAGR-100, which generates and freezes Partner_External_ID__c. Not a blocker: all five Partners already carry theirs, including PT-DIRECT, so the Is Direct formula works today.

Output

Object, fields, four automations and the DLRS rule deployed in the Partial Copy sandbox; metadata retrieved and committed. API names recorded on this ticket. A short operating note recorded on the ticket covering the manual cases above, so whoever picks up a weekly email knows what to do with it.

comments.body:
Hi @Kobi Kunasekaran,

I have few questions:

  1. Do we want to delete the Operator Partner Relationship if either the Operator or Partner is deleted, or should prevent the deletion of either Operator or Partner if it is related to at least one Operator Partner Relationship record?

  2. The reason for choosing a lookup relationship is that there are Direct Partners without an Operator, correct?

@Cedrick Infantado

  1. No deletion if the Operator or Partner is deleted, technically shouldn’t happen anyways but I’d rather we preserve the history. That said, can we turn on history tracking so we are able to see who the original Operator Partner combo is? I think if we have some logic that sets the Operator/Partner combo for the record , like the relationship key for example, can we make sure it doesn’t change when one or the other is deleted or removed from the relevant lookup fields? This way even if the lookup fields are cleared, the ID would remain the same so we know what the original relationship was.

  2. Are you referring to the Operator/Partner lookup fields? If so, this is the standard design for setting up a Junction object no? The idea is that Operator <> Partner is a many to many relationship which we want to capture in this junction object. What are the alternative to lookups would you suggest?

@Kobi Kunasekaran thanks for the answer. Another question.

For Automation 1:

  • Steps: 1. Build the key as Operator__c & "-" & Partner__c. 2. Get Records on Operator_Partner_Relationship__c where Relationship_Key__c equals it. 3. Found → if Status__c = 'Inactive' leave it alone, Automation 2 owns Status. Not found → Create Records with Operator, Partner, Relationship Key, Status Active. 4. Update Records on the triggering Deal setting Relationship__c.

  1. What happen to Deal.Relationship__c if there is an existing Operator_Partner_Relationship__c with Status__c = 'Inactive'? Do I need to still populate the Deal.Relationship__c field?

  2. If yes, I think we don’t need to check the status as we need to populate Deal.Relationship__c either way, right?

fields.description:
## Outcome and context

Once the relationship record holds direct terms, the same values on the Operator record are a second copy of the same fact. Two copies drift, and the one someone edits is not reliably the one a report reads. This moves the values and takes the old location off the page.

One constraint decides the shape of the work: **the billing fields are Account fields shared by both the Operator and Partner record types.** They cannot be deleted — Partner records still use them. Retirement on the Operator side means removing them from the Operator page and blanking the values, not deleting fields.

The same applies to the shared Direct partner Account. Its own billing fields sit on the Partner page it shares with Catena and every other partner, so they cannot be hidden for that one record. Blank them and rely on the field description to say where direct terms now live.

## Current state

Operator records carry populated billing values — the BetMGM record has the full set. `Billing_Relationship__c` is a restricted picklist, `Direct` / `Via Partner`, whose only stated job is controlling which billing fields show on the Operator page.

## Proposed solution

1. Export every Operator with any billing value populated, plus the Direct partner Account, and attach the export to this ticket before touching anything.
2. Ensure each of those Operators has a Direct relationship row — create it by hand where the operator has no direct Deal yet.
3. Copy the values across, field for field, including the address.
4. Blank the billing values on those Operator records and on the Direct partner Account.
5. Remove the billing fields and the Billing Relationship field from the Operator Lightning page and the Operator Account layout.
6. Delete `Billing_Relationship__c` once step 5 has soaked for a period Kobi agrees. It has no remaining job — the section it controlled is gone, and the client's objection was that a single either/or value cannot express an operator that is both direct and via-partner at once. **Confirm this with Kobi before deleting;** the alternative is keeping it as a read-only indicator.
7. Update the Description on the shared billing Account fields to say they apply to Partner records, and that operator direct terms live on the Operator Partner Relationship record.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every Operator that had a billing value has a Direct relationship row carrying the same values, field for field, verified against the pre-move export.
2. No Operator record and not the Direct partner Account retains a populated billing value.
3. Billing values on real Partner records — Catena, GDC, Cipher — are unchanged.
4. The Operator page shows neither the billing section nor the Billing Relationship field.
5. A user with the standard operator permission set can open a migrated Operator and reach its direct billing terms.

## Output

Pre-move export attached to this ticket. Record counts moved, recorded in a completion comment.

## Dependencies

Depends on _Hold direct billing terms on the Direct relationship record_.

Moving direct terms to a child record puts the most common billing task one click further away than it is today. If it does not behave, the fallback is a Dynamic Related List – Single filtered to the Direct row with the billing fields as columns — visible, but read-only in place.

> **Help Text:** Set automatically. Points at this operator's direct billing arrangement.

## Acceptance criteria

2. Editing a value there saves it on the relationship record, and the relationship record shows the change.

fields.description:
Outcome and context

The associated-partner and associated-operator counts on the Account header are derived by concatenating partner record Ids into a 255-character text field and counting the semicolons. Eighteen-character Ids plus a delimiter fill that field at about thirteen entries, after which the value truncates mid-Id and the count silently under-reports. The rollup has no criteria either, so a partner whose deals all closed years ago still counts as associated.

Neither problem is visible yet at 28 deals and four partners. Both become visible as the org fills up, and neither is fixable in the current shape — a distinct count is not something DLRS does. Once relationship rows exist, both numbers are just a count of rows.

Current state

  • Deals_Operator_Associated_Partners — DLRS Concatenate Distinct of Deal__c.Partner__c into Account.Associated_Partners_List__c (Text 255), delimiter ;, Realtime, no relationship criteria. Mirror rule Deals_Partner_Associated_Operators into Associated_Operators_List__c.

  • Account.Associated_Partners__c and Associated_Operators__c are formula fields counting semicolons + 1, so they cannot be the target of a rollup.

Proposed solution

  1. Two DLRS Count rules on the relationship object into Account — one keyed on Operator, one on Partner — with criteria Status__c = 'Active'. The Operator-side rule also carries Is_Direct__c = false, so the shared Direct record is not counted as one of an operator's partners.

  2. Replace the formula count fields. A formula field cannot be a rollup target, so each has to be deleted and recreated as Number. To keep the same API names — and avoid touching the header components and any report or list view referencing them — erase the deleted field from the deleted-fields list before recreating; the name is not available until it is erased. Recreating under a new name is the fallback and costs a downstream sweep.

  3. Deactivate and remove the two Concatenate Distinct rules and the two list text fields once the new counts are confirmed correct.

Acceptance criteria

  1. An Operator with twenty active partner relationships shows twenty.

  2. An Operator whose relationships are all Inactive shows zero.

  3. An Operator with a direct arrangement and two partners shows two, not three.

  4. Deactivating a relationship reduces the Operator's count with no edit to the Account.

  5. The Account header and every report or list view that referenced the old count still resolves after the change.

Out of scope

Whether the Direct partner Account should display an operator count at all — a display decision for Kobi, not a build change.

Dependencies

Depends on Operator–Partner Relationship records created and deactivated from Deals.

Supersedes the associated-partner and associated-operator header rollups as originally built; link the earlier header-rollup tickets to this one.

Outcome and context

Users looking at the Operator or Partner record page see a count in the Highlights Panel — Associated Partners and Associated Sources on Operator, Associated Operators and Associated Sources on Partner — with nothing explaining what is being counted. Kobi raised this while reviewing the rollups with Taryn on 2026-09-11: the fields need help text in the highlights panel so a user can tell what they represent without asking.

Current state

  • Operator: Associated_Partners__c (Number, Formula) and Operator_Associated_Sources__c (Number, Formula), both built in BUILD-272, sit on the Operator Dynamic Highlights Panel with no Field Description or Help Text set.

  • Partner: Associated_Operators__c and Associated_Sources__c (Number, Formula), both built in BUILD-265, sit on the Partner Dynamic Highlights Panel with the same gap.

  • All four are read-only, DLRS-backed distinct counts of related Deal records — Operator's two fields count distinct Partners and distinct Sources across its Deals; Partner's two fields count distinct Operators and distinct Sources across its Deals.

Proposed solution

  1. Add a Field Description and Help Text to each of the four fields, so the text a user sees on hover in the Highlights Panel explains what is being counted.

  2. Field Description and Help Text (ready to paste):

Associated_Partners__c (Operator) — Description: Count of distinct Partners across this Operator's related Deals. Maintained by DLRS — do not edit directly. Help Text: Number of different partners this operator has deals with.

Operator_Associated_Sources__c (Operator) — Description: Count of distinct Sources across this Operator's related Deals. Maintained by DLRS — do not edit directly. Help Text: Number of different deal sources tied to this operator.

Associated_Operators__c (Partner) — Description: Count of distinct Operators across this Partner's related Deals. Maintained by DLRS — do not edit directly. Help Text: Number of different operators this partner has deals with.

Associated_Sources__c (Partner) — Description: Count of distinct Sources across this Partner's related Deals. Maintained by DLRS — do not edit directly. Help Text: Number of different deal sources tied to this partner.

  1. No change to the underlying DLRS rules, the helper list fields, or the count formulas — this ticket only touches Description and Help Text on the four visible fields.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Hovering the info icon on Associated Partners and Associated Sources in the Operator Highlights Panel shows the help text above.

  2. Hovering the info icon on Associated Operators and Associated Sources in the Partner Highlights Panel shows the help text above.

  3. No other field, layout, DLRS rule, or formula is changed.

Out of scope

Resolving the open questions carried on BUILD-272 / BUILD-265 — whether the Deal scope is all Deals or Active-only, and how a blank Source is counted. Both stay open on their original tickets; the wording above is deliberately scope-agnostic so it does not need revisiting once those are answered.

Source

Wagertech Internal Sync, Sep 11, 2026 — Kobi asked Taryn whether help text could be added to the Highlights Panel for the associated sources and associated partners rollups; Taryn confirmed it was possible. Restated as a next step in the Sep 14, 2026 sync notes.
