**Summary**
Reps track referral payments on a sheet tab for each BA. Salesforce already calculates a payout amount on each Sign-Up and has a Payment Sent checkbox. It has no way to batch payments, record a transfer, or stop a double payment.

At the Sep 25 discovery call, the launch scope was set to **referral payouts only**. BA commissions and player payouts stay outside Salesforce at launch.

**Requirements captured (Sep 25 call)**

* At Sign-Up logging, the payout type and currency default from the Referrer. The rep can override them.
* The rep selects several unpaid Sign-Ups for one referrer. The system creates a Payout record with the total amount.
* A batch holds one currency only.
* **Cash:** the rep marks the Payout as Paid, with Date Sent and the BMO transaction ID. A Paid Payout is locked.
* **Bet credit:** the rep splits the total into smaller redeposit records for the referrer. These follow the redeposit proof process. The Payout status follows the status of its redeposits.
* **Secondary referrer:** a one-time bonus after 10 eligible Sign-Ups. A flag on the Referrer shows eligibility. The system does **not** create the Payout automatically. A per-referral flag excludes a referral from the secondary count.
* **Fraud:** a fraud-flagged Sign-Up is visible in the queue but cannot be selected. A confirmed-fraud Sign-Up does not show in the queue. Before Paid, the rep can remove a flagged Sign-Up from the batch. After Paid, see the "Write-offs and clawbacks for paid Sign-Ups" ticket.
* Keep the UI simple for rep adoption.

**Open questions**

* Secondary bonus amount: $100 cash / $200 bet credit, or $250 bet credit (Joyce, Jul 17)? _(Lina)_
* Rate basis: the org matrix uses currency and type, but the PRD says operator / vertical / tier. Also 4 of the 8 matrix rows are in no document. _(Lina)_
* Naming: "Bet Credit" or "Redeposit"? The matrix has no Redeposit type.
* Payout status values. Who can mark a Payout as Paid?
* Can Ops override a Sign-Up's payout amount? (Lina, Sep 1)
* How do we tag Sign-Ups that were already paid before launch?
* Is there a payout frequency by market?

**Done when**

* Joyce's workflow diagram (Slack, Sep 23) is reconciled with the design.
* WagerTech reviews the design, and the outcome is on this ticket.
* The build stories exist and link to this card (under a Payouts epic, if one is created).
* WAGR-109, 110, 111, 359 and 377 are repurposed or closed. WAGR-111 is a placeholder but sits in Ready — move it back.

fields.description:
## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Normal users see Deal Status as read-only and change lifecycle state through controlled actions/automation.

## Status baseline

Draft, Active, Paused, Inactive, Closed, Archived.

* Review Required is removed.
* Archived is terminal.
* WAGR-506 owns the picklist value set/default.

## Status UI / access

* Do not expose the real Status field as writable on page layouts, Lightning record pages, inline edit or guided edit surfaces.
* Where Status is displayed on the Deal UI, use the read-only Status display/formula field.
* Use ordinary FLS / Permission Set access to keep the underlying Status field non-editable to normal users.
* Do not add duplicate Custom Permission checks inside every Flow unless a concrete bypass path requires one.
* Lifecycle actions may use Permission Set-controlled visibility for access distribution.

## Controlled actions

* Activate — WAGR-450.
* Pause — this story.
* Reactivate — this story for Paused/Inactive; Closed has additional behavior in its dedicated story.
* Close — dedicated Closed behavior story.
* Archive — WAGR-447.

### Pause

On confirmation:

* Status → Paused.
* Mark all currently Active Affiliate Links inactive.
* Preserve enough state to know exactly which Links were Active immediately before Pause.
* Do not alter DRAs.
* Queue CMS sync through the common mechanism.

**Confirmation copy:**

> Pausing this Deal will mark all currently active Affiliate Links inactive in Salesforce and queue the changes to sync to the CMS. Links that were already inactive will stay inactive. When this Deal is reactivated, only Links that were active before the pause will be restored.

### Reactivate from Paused

* Status → Active.
* Clear Effective End Date through shared Active-entry logic.
* Restore only the Affiliate Links that were Active immediately before Pause.
* Links that were already inactive before Pause remain inactive.
* Do not alter DRAs.
* Queue CMS sync.

### Inactive

* Inactive is automated/informational only.
* Reactivation may occur automatically from qualifying activity.
* Inactive itself does not deactivate Links or alter DRAs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Normal users cannot directly edit source Deal Status on supported user surfaces.
2. Status shown on Deal UI uses the read-only display/formula field.
3. Pause deactivates only currently Active Links and preserves pre-pause active state.
4. Paused → Active restores only the preserved active Link set.
5. Pause/reactivate do not change DRAs.
6. Inactive has no Link/DRA side effects.
7. Archived never appears in normal Reactivate.
8. Shared lifecycle tracking and CMS sync remain centralized.
fields.summary: Deal — Lifecycle status controls and controlled actions

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Centralize Deal lifecycle dates/history so action flows only change Status and shared automation owns tracking.

## Fields

Use Date fields:

* Previous Deal Status;
* Draft Date;
* First Activated Date;
* Active Date;
* Paused Date;
* Inactive Date;
* Closed Date;
* Archived Date;
* Effective End Date.

Review Required Date and Retired Date are no longer part of the target lifecycle.

## Rules

* On normal Deal creation in Draft, stamp Draft Date if blank.
* Preserve an authorized historical Draft Date supplied for migration/remediation.
* Previous Status + destination Date update only when Status actually changes.
* First Activated Date is write-once.
* Active Date updates on each actual transition to Active.
* Entering Closed stamps Closed Date + Effective End Date.
* Entering Archived stamps Archived Date + Effective End Date through shared end-state logic.
* **Any transition to Active clears Effective End Date.**
* Unrelated edits do not restamp lifecycle Dates.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New Draft gets Draft Date once.
2. Active → Paused stamps Paused Date.
3. Paused → Active updates Active Date, preserves First Activated Date and clears Effective End Date.
4. Active → Closed stamps Closed Date + Effective End Date.
5. Closed → Active clears Effective End Date.
6. Eligible state → Archived stamps Archived Date + Effective End Date.
7. API/data-load transitions receive the same centralized lifecycle treatment.
fields.summary: Deal — Lifecycle status tracking, Date fields and Effective End Date

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Active Deals with no qualifying activity for the configured number of calendar days become Inactive through a simple scheduled sweep.

## Eligibility

* First Activated Date + Last Sign-Up First Click Date determine the activity baseline.
* Default threshold = 90 days, configurable.
* Exactly N days old remains Active; older than N days qualifies.
* Only current Status = Active can qualify.

## Inactive behavior

* Scheduled Flow sets Status = Inactive.
* WAGR-486 stamps lifecycle tracking.
* WAGR-455 queues the status sync.
* **Inactive is informational only.**
* Do not deactivate Affiliate Links.
* Do not alter DRAs.
* CMS may store/display Inactive but must not treat it like Pause.
* Qualifying new activity may return the Deal to Active through WAGR-498.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Draft/Paused/Closed/Archived/Inactive Deals never qualify.
2. 90-day boundary behavior remains as designed.
3. Inactivation sends the new status but leaves Affiliate Links and DRAs unchanged.
4. The scheduled flow performs no per-Deal Sign-Up query.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Ops can report first-click activity occurring while a Deal is currently in a non-live lifecycle state without adding durable event snapshots in V1.

## States to flag

At minimum:

* Draft;
* Paused;
* Closed;
* Archived.

Inactive normally auto-reactivates. If qualifying activity exists after Inactive Date while the Deal remains Inactive, surface that as an automation exception.

## Rules

* Compare Sign-Up First Click Date to the Date the parent Deal entered its current lifecycle state.
* Same-date activity remains reviewable because lifecycle fields intentionally use Date, not DateTime.
* Do not block Sign-Up creation solely because parent Deal is Draft/Paused/Closed/Archived.
* Review Required and Retired are not part of the current lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria

1. First Click on/after Archived Date is reportable while parent Deal remains Archived.
2. Same behavior for Draft, Paused and Closed using matching lifecycle Dates.
3. Qualifying activity left on Inactive can be flagged as an automation exception.
4. No durable status-at-arrival snapshot is required for V1.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Operator/Partner integration identifiers cannot be changed casually after they have participated in an activated Deal, while legitimate exceptional remediation remains possible through an admin-controlled process.

## Requirements

Protect integration identity fields such as:

* `Operator_External_ID__c`
* `Partner_External_ID__c`
* `Partner_Code__c`
* equivalent fields approved during grooming.

Standard users must not be able to edit these fields through normal UI/API paths when the Account has any related Deal whose **First Activated Date is populated**.

Do not use current Deal Status = Active; Paused/Inactive/Closed/Retired Deals still count as having been activated.

## Recommended durable marker

Maintain a system-managed Account-level Boolean equivalent to **Has Ever Activated Deal**.

* Source event: the first related Deal successfully crosses first activation.
* Once TRUE, it does not clear because Deals later become Paused/Inactive/Closed/Retired.
* Unrelated Deal updates do not rewrite/toggle it.
* Do not use existing “Active Deal count” DLRS fields as a substitute; those answer a different current-state question.

Legitimate correction uses an explicit privileged/manual admin remediation workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Operator with an ever-activated Deal cannot have its integration External ID edited by a standard user.
2. Partner with an ever-activated Deal cannot have Partner External ID / Partner Code edited by a standard user.
3. Account with only never-activated Deals can still follow the approved maintenance process.
4. First Deal activation sets the durable marker once.
5. Later status changes/unrelated Deal edits do not clear or restamp the marker.
6. Admin remediation is explicit and auditable rather than achieved by ordinary record Edit.

fields.description:
## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Every Affiliate Link has a stable cross-system identifier that survives ordinary Link Code edits and can be referenced by CMS/SLC without relying only on Salesforce record Id.

## Requirements

* Add a system-managed Link External ID field.
* Logical value = **Deal External ID + deterministic delimiter + Link Code**.
* Do not use Salesforce record Id as part of this external identifier.
* Configure as Text(255), Unique and External ID (or the closest final metadata shape that preserves those constraints).
* Generate on creation, or when blank and all required source values exist.
* Once populated, ordinary Link Code edits do not automatically regenerate Link External ID.
* Exceptional regeneration requires an authorized admin to intentionally clear it; automation then regenerates from current Deal External ID + Link Code.
* Add `link_external_id` to CMS `links[]` in addition to `sf_link_id`.
* Before enabling uniqueness, run a data-quality check that Link Code is unique within each target Deal.
* Never silently truncate the composed identifier.
* WAGR-499 must confirm the final Link Code length policy. The composed Deal External ID + delimiter + Link Code must fit within 255 characters.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Same Link Code on two different Deals produces different Link External IDs.
2. Ordinary Link Code edit does not silently change external identity.
3. Authorized clear/regenerate produces the new value from current source fields.
4. Normal users cannot directly edit Link External ID.
5. CMS payload carries both `sf_link_id` and `link_external_id`.
6. Overlength composed identity is rejected clearly; it is never truncated.
7. Final approved Link Code maximum is compatible with the 255-character Link External ID envelope.

## Dependencies

* WAGR-499 — Link Code / Tracking URL storage hardening.
* WAGR-456 — CMS Link payload.

## External dependency

Kobi must inform Strah so CMS stores/returns `link_external_id` on click/SLC events and, where practical, later DRA events.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Ops can intentionally keep Links out of CMS and previously-published Link history is preserved safely.

## Current V1 rules

* Add/use generic **Exclude from CMS**.
* Never-published Link may be deleted through the guided confirmation path.
* Published Active Link cannot be deleted/excluded.
* Published Link must first be Inactive and CMS must have successfully confirmed the inactive state before omission/delete could become eligible.
* Until CMS omission semantics are confirmed, do not enable production omission-based deletion/exclusion for previously-published Links.
* Do not add a deleted/tombstone payload state unless CMS requires it.
* Direct/API delete and re-parenting must obey the same protection.

## Lifecycle interaction

* Pause/Close/Archive may make currently Active Links inactive through Deal lifecycle actions.
* Inactive Deal status does **not** change Links.
* Whether Affiliate Links themselves gain an explicit **Archived** status is intentionally **out of scope here** and tracked in the separate Link Archive follow-up.
* If Link Archived is adopted, revisit this story's physical-delete/end-of-life rules rather than silently layering a second lifecycle.

## Publication markers

Keep lightweight system-managed publication state sufficient to prove last successful CMS state. These are not a separate Link retry engine.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Never-published Link can be deleted after confirmation.
2. Published Active Link cannot be deleted/excluded.
3. Published inactive Link is not omission/delete-eligible until CMS has confirmed inactive.
4. API/UI paths cannot bypass protection.
5. Deal Pause/Close/Archive deactivation does not make a Link delete-eligible merely because a request was queued; successful CMS confirmation is still required.

## Outcome

Reduce the immediate risk of accidental Sign-Up changes/deletions while preserving the existing guided Screen Flow paths.

## Requirements

* Remove Sign-Up **Delete** access from normal WagerTech personas.
* Keep System Administrator / deliberate admin delete capability for remediation.
* Confirm normal users do not have **Edit Read Only Fields**.
* Review Sign-Up standard page-layout / Dynamic Forms editability so Rep users cannot directly edit protected fields through standard UI paths.
* Preserve the existing guided Screen Flows, including any flows using Salesforce Record Field components that depend on underlying Edit CRUD/FLS.
* Where Ops / Managers legitimately need direct edit access (for example Fraud / Archive sections), capture that as explicit persona requirements rather than opening broad Sign-Up edit access.

## Validation

Test as a Rep user:

* list-view row Edit cannot change protected fields;
* inline edit cannot change protected fields;
* record-page direct edit cannot change protected fields;
* Delete is unavailable;
* existing Log Sign Up / Complete Sign Up / other approved Screen Flow actions still work.

## Related

* WAGR-436
* WAGR-449
* Working plan: https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/268730374/WagerTech+Access+Permission+Model+Working+Plan

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Each Deal exposes the latest historical **first-click Date** across its related Sign-Ups so inactivity qualification can be evaluated without querying Sign-Up history inside the scheduled Flow.

## Source field

WAGR-498 owns `Sign_Up__c.First_Click_Date__c` (final API name subject to metadata conventions).

This is a **Date**, not DateTime, because Deal activity/inactivity is a calendar-day business rule.

## Implementation direction

Prefer a realtime/appropriate DLRS or equivalent roll-up:

* Parent: Deal.
* Child: Sign-Up.
* Aggregate: **MAX(First Click Date)**.
* Target: Deal system-managed Date conceptually named `Last_Signup_First_Click_Date__c`.

This replaces the previously-proposed copied `Deal_Stamp_Last_Activity` subflow.

Why:

* preserves historical/imported first-click dates;
* recalculates correctly when a Sign-Up is deliberately re-parented;
* avoids per-Sign-Up whole-Deal updates;
* makes the value visible/reportable for WAGR-487.

## Source-event rule

The rollup changes only because the underlying related Sign-Up set / First Click Dates change.

* Unrelated Deal updates do not change it.
* Unrelated Sign-Up edits do not change First Click Date and therefore do not advance activity.
* Repeat clicks rolled into the same Sign-Up do not update First Click Date in V1.
* If a Sign-Up is re-parented, source/destination rollups recalculate while the Sign-Up's First Click Date remains preserved.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Deal with no related Sign-Up First Click Date has blank Last Sign-Up First Click Date.
2. First qualifying Sign-Up rolls its First Click Date to the Deal.
3. Later Sign-Up with a newer First Click Date advances the Deal value.
4. Older/equal Sign-Up does not advance the MAX value.
5. Unrelated Sign-Up edit does not change First Click Date or Deal Last Sign-Up First Click Date.
6. Re-parenting a Sign-Up recalculates both affected Deals without changing the Sign-Up's historical First Click Date.
7. Existing Player Last Activity automation remains unchanged.

## Dependencies

* WAGR-498 — Sign-Up First Click Date semantics and source-event behavior.
* WAGR-487 — scheduled inactivity consumes this Deal field.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Each Sign-Up preserves the calendar Date of its first click, and only a qualifying new/re-parented Sign-Up source event can automatically reactivate an Inactive Deal.

## First Click Date

Add a system-managed Sign-Up **First Click Date** (final API name TBD).

Use **Date**, not DateTime, for this derived business field.

### SLC-created Sign-Up

* The inbound SLC already stores the source click as `Study_Link_Click__c.Click_Timestamp__c` (UTC DateTime).
* When a **new Sign-Up record is first created from an SLC**, stamp First Click Date from the **UTC calendar date** contained in that source click timestamp.
* This avoids running-user timezone differences.

Example:
`2026-10-01T00:30:00Z` → First Click Date = `2026-10-01`.

### Repeat clicks

* Multiple SLC clicks may roll into the same existing Sign-Up.
* Repeat clicks do **not** restamp First Click Date in V1.
* A future Last Click Date / repeat-click activity rule is explicitly out of scope.

### Import/manual exception

* Authorized historical import/remediation may explicitly supply First Click Date.
* Preserve a supplied historical value.
* If a legitimate non-SLC Sign-Up is created without a supplied historical first-click date, default the field to the record's creation business date.
* Once populated, ordinary updates do not restamp it.

### Re-parenting

* If an existing Sign-Up's Deal lookup is deliberately moved to another Deal, preserve First Click Date.
* Do not use re-parent time or LastModifiedDate as the activity date.

## Deal auto-reactivation

Trigger/evaluate only from these source events:

1. a new Sign-Up is created with a related Deal; or
2. an existing Sign-Up's Deal lookup changes to a different Deal.

Do **not** trigger reactivation merely because an unrelated Sign-Up field or Deal field changed.

For the destination Deal:

* Active → no status change.
* Inactive → set Active only when First Click Date is populated and **First Click Date >= Inactive Date**.
* New / Paused / Closed / Review Required / Retired → do not auto-activate/reactivate.
* If Inactive Date is unexpectedly blank, fail safe / do not auto-reactivate; surface for remediation rather than guessing.

WAGR-486 owns Previous Status / Active Date / lifecycle stamping for the resulting status transition.  
WAGR-455 owns the resulting CMS sync request.

## Activity summary

WAGR-497 separately rolls MAX(Sign-Up First Click Date) to the Deal. Reactivation must not be driven solely by a generic parent rollup-field update; it is tied to the Sign-Up source events above.

## Existing Player automation

Do not modify WAGR-72 Player automation. Player status continues to use its existing Completed-signup semantics; Deal activity uses First Click Date.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New SLC-created Sign-Up stamps UTC-derived First Click Date once.
2. Repeat click into the same Sign-Up does not change First Click Date or auto-reactivate a Deal by itself.
3. Unrelated Sign-Up edit does not change First Click Date or trigger Deal reactivation.
4. Authorized import-supplied First Click Date is preserved.
5. Re-parented Sign-Up preserves First Click Date.
6. New/re-parented Sign-Up to Inactive Deal with First Click Date on/after Inactive Date → Active.
7. Same event with First Click Date before Inactive Date → remains Inactive.
8. New/re-parented Sign-Up to Paused/Closed/Retired/New/Review Required → no automatic status change.
9. Player status automation behavior remains unchanged.
10. WAGR-497 Deal rollup reflects the preserved First Click Date.

## Dependencies

* WAGR-486 — lifecycle Dates/status tracking.
* WAGR-497 — Deal Last Sign-Up First Click Date rollup.
* WAGR-455 — CMS sync after a resulting Deal status change.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Affiliate Link source fields can store the authoritative values required by CMS without silent truncation, while the Link External ID remains deterministic and within Salesforce limits.

## Current-state finding

The Partial Sandbox metadata sweep found:

* `Link_Code__c` is currently Text(40).
* the current Tracking URL field is a Salesforce URL field, which is limited to 255 characters.
* source/Airtable data includes tracking URLs substantially longer than 255 characters.

## Requirements

### Tracking URL

* The authoritative Tracking URL used by CMS must support the CMS contract envelope of up to 2,048 characters.
* Do not silently truncate an existing/source URL.
* Replace/augment the current URL-field storage with a field type/length that can preserve the full authoritative URL.
* Preserve an easy clickable user experience where practical (for example a display/action/formula pattern), but clickability must not reduce the authoritative storage length.
* Update the existing Affiliate Link create/edit experience to use the authoritative field.
* Migration/cutover must copy current valid values to the authoritative field before the old field is deprecated.

### Link Code

* Do not silently truncate Link Code.
* Current design may retain the existing 40-character operational limit **if WagerTech confirms Link Code is intended to be a short controlled code**.
* Legacy/source rows that exceed the approved limit must be deliberately normalized/re-created with an approved Salesforce-friendly code before migration.
* If WagerTech confirms longer Link Codes are valid business values, expand the field before migration and re-check WAGR-490 Link External ID length.
* No runtime architecture is required solely to preserve arbitrary legacy Airtable token values.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A Tracking URL longer than 255 characters and within the approved CMS maximum is stored in full and sent without truncation.
2. Existing valid Tracking URLs are migrated to the authoritative field.
3. The Affiliate Link edit flow reads/writes the authoritative Tracking URL field.
4. Link Code values that exceed the approved maximum fail clearly or are resolved during migration; they are never silently truncated.
5. WAGR-490 verifies the composed Link External ID still fits its Salesforce field after the final Link Code limit is confirmed.

## Dependencies / sequencing

* Must be resolved before production Link migration/publication.
* WAGR-456 depends on the authoritative Link Code/Tracking URL fields.
* WAGR-490 depends on the final Link Code limit.
* Lower priority than the core Deal lifecycle/CMS sender foundation, but required before Affiliate Links go live.

fields.description:
Outcome and context

Ops users need to see which Brand Ambassador (BA) owns each Sign-Up without opening the record and going to the More Info (Ops) tab. Emily asked on 2026-09-30 how to filter the full "All" Sign-Ups list to one BA's signups in split view, and said the BA tag needs to be "more prevalent" in the Ops view. She also asked that this go on the agenda for the same-day call. This ticket captures the visibility change. It is Ops-only by intent, and that still needs to be confirmed (see Open questions).

Current state

  • Brand Ambassador is a lookup field on Sign-Up. It sits on the More Info (Ops) tab, under General Information.

  • The split view list cards show Player, Operator, Status and Created time. The Sign-Up highlights panel shows Operator, Partner, Market Country, Market State, Vertical, Status, Proof Status and Completion. BA is on neither.

  • Split view does not support filtering or sorting. Users must filter in table view, then switch back to split view. The filter stays applied. Emily has this answer.

  • The BA filter value is a plain text box, not a picklist, because BA is a lookup field. Emily asked if it could be a picklist. Standard list view filters do not offer that for a lookup field.

  • Emily's column template lists 22 columns (Player through Notes) for the "All Sign-Ups" list view. It has two notes: freeze up to column G (Country), and "In the OPS View we need to see the BA Tag as well." The template does not say which columns are Ops-only.

  • Related work: WAGR-423 covers the Sign-Up list views ("All Active", sort order and column alignment). This ticket builds on those lists and should not start before the WAGR-423 column set is final.

Proposed solution

Options to review. None is decided yet.

  1. Add Brand Ambassador as a column on an Ops-only Sign-Up list view. In split view, only the first four list fields show on the cards, so BA must sit in the first four columns to appear there.

  2. Add Brand Ambassador to the Sign-Up highlights panel or compact layout for Ops. Compact layouts are assigned by record type, not by profile, so an Ops-only header needs a separate Lightning record page assigned to the Ops profile. The exact approach is not confirmed.

  3. Restrict the BA field with field-level security to Ops profiles or an Ops permission set. FLS is the reliable control. Sharing a list view with the Ops group only controls who sees that list view.

Acceptance criteria (draft, pending confirmation)

  1. An Ops user sees the Brand Ambassador name in the Ops Sign-Up list view without opening the record.

  2. Non-Ops users (BAs and Reps) do not see the BA column or field, if Ops-only is confirmed.

  3. Existing list views for other users are not changed.

  4. The change is checked in split view and in table view.

Open questions

  • Where should BA be more prominent: the list, the record header, or both? Emily was asked or will be asked on the call.

  • Should BA be Ops-only? Emily's template says BA is added "in the OPS View." It does not say BAs or Reps must not see it.

  • Which of Emily's 22 template columns are Ops-only? The template does not say.

  • Can Lightning freeze columns up to column G? Not confirmed. This is not a standard list view setting as far as we know.

  • Is a BA picklist filter needed? If yes, options are saved list views per BA, or custom work. Custom work is a separate ticket.

Out of scope

  • Freezing columns (until confirmed possible).

  • Building a BA picklist filter or a custom filter component.

  • The "All Active" list view, sort order and Recently Viewed alignment (WAGR-423).

Source

  • Emily Vandenberg, Slack thread in the WagerTech channel, 2026-09-30, 9:51 AM to 10:28 AM: https://jumpr-solutions.slack.com/archives/C0BBC05C2HG/p1790776304286699

  • Emily's column template (Table View - Column Template): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sljtqwg7PL7OeLT6HKvjnXW9EC-70v9t5wo74cCwgjo/edit?gid=0

  • Salesforce Ben, "Your Complete Guide to Salesforce Split View" (filter and sort only in table view): https://www.salesforceben.com/your-complete-guide-to-salesforce-split-view/

  • Related: WAGR-423, parent epic WAGR-305.

comments.body:
@Cedrick Infantado , quick check before I reply to Emily. She asked if the BA filter value in the Sign-Ups list view can be a picklist instead of a text box.

BA is a lookup, so I think the filter just gives a plain text box (type the name) and there's no dropdown option.

Is that right, or is there a way to get a dropdown that I'm missing? If not, I was going to offer saved list views per BA.

@Taryn Reithofer Yeah, you’re right. Since this is a lookup field, the only option is to have a text box in that filter.

How many BAs do they have? I’m worried that the list view would be too long.
@Cedrick Infantado Well not a lot looking at the test data but I’d have to ask what it would be in prod.
@Kobi Kunasekaran I learnt about this nifty filtering value! Where it points to the current user, but the thing is that BA’s don’t have table view edit access so they can’t point to themselves here.
But I guess this doesn’t make sense either way because Ops are searching for BA’s and not BA’s searching from themselves…
SORRY I’m feeling spammy I guess. I found some workarounds online but it would be a large lift. I’ll let Emily know and see what she says, perhaps it a V2 enhancement.

@Taryn Reithofer The $USER filter is something we will do as additional list views for only the lists Reps need to see. Once you finalize the columns, we’d basically clone and call it My New Signs Ups, My In Progress Sign Ups, etc. add the $USER filter to those. Those will be the list views Reps should have access to. Generally they shouldn’t have access to the all rep views, which we can control from the Sharing settings of those list views, we’ve left these open intentionally for now.

So if the underlying ask is that Reps should be able to easily see their assigned Sign Ups, we can do that without them needing to filter things manually.

If Ops wants an easy way to filter for specific reps with standard layouts, it’s unfortunately using the annoying filters. We can potentially make it a bit easier later through some hacks but it’ll require a small build + add some maintenance when new reps are added. This or we build reports if the point of what they need is for reporting and not necessarily for logging sign ups like reps.

## Outcome and context

## Proposed solution

Options to review. None is decided yet.

fields.description:
**Context** While testing WAGR-427 (streamlined referrer creation), the "Log Sign Up" flow showed the record type selection screen (Operator / Partner / Player / Referrer) when adding a new referrer. Two findings came out of the discussion.

1. **Record type options are controlled at profile level, not per view.** The record type picker is not configurable per screen. Admins always see all record types. For Reps, options are limited through the profile. (Jared Ali, via the WT Rep PSG, is the test user.)
2. **Some Rep users do not see the sign-up action buttons.** Andy Bhiekham has the same PSG setup as Jared Ali, but the sign-up action buttons do not show. Cedrick confirmed the fix: tick the **Flow User** checkbox on the User record.

Not a bug. This is a config gap that could cause wrong test results and a confusing Rep experience.

**Requirements**

* Review every active Rep user in the sandbox and confirm **Flow User** is ticked.
* Fix any Rep user where it is not ticked.
* Confirm the record type options each Rep user sees match what is expected for their profile.
* Log which users were changed (input for the later full permissions check).

**Why now**
Emily can now log in as other users to test. We do not want her testing with a user we have not configured yet.

**Out of scope**

* The bigger permissions review planned for later.
* Changing the record type picker behaviour (covered by WAGR-427).

**Open questions / assumptions**

* Assumption: sandbox only for now. Confirm whether production needs the same check before go-live.
* Unknown: expected record type set per Rep profile. Confirm with Cedrick/Emily if unclear.

**Related**

* WAGR-427: Referrer: Streamline new referrer creation flow

fields.description:
Summary

Set the final Deal Status value list once so lifecycle stories consume a single field definition.

Final values

Order

API value

Label

Meaning

1

Draft

Draft

Being set up; default; never sent to CMS.

2

Active

Active

Salesforce has activated/intends the Deal to be live. CMS Sync Status separately shows whether CMS accepted the latest state.

3

Paused

Paused

Temporary operational pause; lifecycle action hides/deactivates active Links and can later restore the pre-pause active set.

4

Inactive

Inactive

Automated informational state after inactivity threshold; does not deactivate Links or alter DRAs.

5

Closed

Closed

Longer-term locked state; reactivatable by permitted users.

6

Archived

Archived

Terminal; never normally reactivated; releases makeup.

Deactivate Review Required rather than delete it.

Requirements

  • Keep restricted picklist and field history.

  • Set Draft as default.

  • API values are exactly Draft, Active, Paused, Inactive, Closed, Archived.

  • Verify the actual deployed metadata uses Archived spelling.

  • Review Required is inactive and cannot be newly set through normal UI/API.

  • This story defines values only; behavior belongs to lifecycle action stories.

Important semantic clarification

  • Active does not mean CMS sync succeeded. Active may coexist with CMS Sync Status = Failed/Retrying.

  • Inactive is informational only. CMS must not interpret it as Pause/hide Links merely because the status value is Inactive.

Out of scope

  • Archive action/makeup release.

  • Closed locking/reactivation behavior.

  • Pause Link-state restoration.

  • CMS contract implementation.

## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Provide a controlled New Deal Screen Flow that creates a Deal in Draft with only the agreed setup fields, previews/validates the input, and can optionally hand off to the separate Commercial Terms flow after the Deal has committed.

## Deal Information

Required:

* Operator — lookup only; do not allow Operator creation.
* Partner — lookup only; do not allow Partner creation.
* Market Country.
* Vertical.
* Source.
* Deal Currency.
* Deal Effective Start Date.

Optional:

* Market State — blank means country-wide.
* Priority Tier.
* Notes.

## Defaults

* Deal Status = Draft from field default; do not expose Status as an input.
* Deal Currency:

    * United States → USD;
    * Canada → CAD;
    * otherwise org default;
    * apply only while Currency is blank; do not silently overwrite a user-selected Currency.
    
* Deal Effective Start Date defaults to today.
* Do not invent future-date activation/scheduling behavior.

## Independent business dimensions

Source and Partner are independent:

* Source = Direct describes how WagerTech sourced the Deal.
* Partner = Direct means no external Partner participates in that Deal.
* Never derive one from the other.

## Optional Commercial Terms handoff

Add checkbox: **Add Commercial Terms**.

If selected:

1. Create/commit the Deal first.
2. Launch the independent Add/Edit Commercial Terms Screen Flow.
3. Pass the new Deal Id.
4. A Commercial Terms error must not roll back Deal creation.

The checkbox may be implemented as a placeholder now or completed by the Commercial Terms epic.

## Optional replacement section

Near the bottom:

* checkbox: **This Deal Replaces an Archived Deal**
* Archived Deal lookup shown/required only when checked.
* After new Deal creation, update the canonical old Deal `Superseded_By__c` relationship.
* Do not persist redundant forward/reverse lookups unless a reporting requirement later justifies both.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New Deal is created as Draft.
2. Operator/Partner cannot be created from their lookup controls.
3. Market State is optional.
4. Currency and Effective Start defaults behave as defined.
5. Source and Partner remain independent.
6. Replacement lookup is required only when replacement checkbox is selected and only returns Archived Deals.
7. Add Commercial Terms runs only after successful Deal commit and cannot roll back Deal creation.
fields.summary: Deal — Guided New Deal creation flow (Draft + optional Commercial Terms handoff)

fields.description:
## Source of truth

https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

## Outcome

Define Closed as a longer-term operational stop that reuses the Archived locked-state restrictions where practical, but keeps the Deal reactivatable and keeps its makeup reserved.

## Enter Closed

Through a controlled Close Deal action:

* show confirmation;
* Status → Closed;
* stamp Closed Date + Effective End Date through shared lifecycle tracking;
* keep raw Makeup Key reserved;
* apply the common locked-state business-field restrictions used by Archived where practical;
* mark all currently Active Affiliate Links inactive;
* queue the resulting Deal snapshot to CMS;
* do not alter DRAs.

**Confirmation copy:**

> Closing this Deal will lock it and mark all currently active Affiliate Links inactive in Salesforce. The changes will be queued to the CMS. Reactivating the Deal will not automatically reactivate its Affiliate Links.

## Reactivate from Closed

* Show Reactivate only to permitted users using practical Permission Set/action visibility.
* Status → Active.
* Shared lifecycle logic clears Effective End Date.
* Makeup remains the same Deal/External Deal ID.
* Affiliate Links remain inactive in V1; do not restore the pre-close active set automatically.
* Do not alter DRAs.
* Queue CMS sync.

## Closed vs Archived

Shared:

* normal business fields locked;
* system/integration/audit fields may still update;
* end-state date behavior;
* active Links are shut off.

Different:

* Closed keeps makeup reserved.
* Closed can Reactivate.
* Archived releases makeup and never uses normal Reactivate.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Close locks normal business editing but preserves system/integration updates.
2. Close stamps Closed Date + Effective End Date.
3. Active Links become inactive; already inactive Links stay inactive.
4. Close does not change DRAs.
5. Closed keeps the raw Makeup Key reserved.
6. Closed → Active clears Effective End Date.
7. Closed → Active does not automatically reactivate Affiliate Links in V1.
8. Archived has no Reactivate action.

fields.description:
## Purpose

Capture the explicit follow-up for tomorrow's WagerTech review: decide whether Affiliate Links need their own terminal **Archived** state rather than relying only on Active/Inactive + Exclude from CMS.

## Current interim behavior

Until this decision changes it:

* Deal Pause deactivates currently Active Links and may restore the pre-pause active set.
* Deal Close deactivates currently Active Links; Closed → Active leaves them inactive.
* Deal Archive deactivates currently Active Links.
* Deal Inactive does not change Links.
* Previously-published Links remain in the full current eligible snapshot until CMS omission semantics are confirmed.

## If Link Archived is adopted, reconcile as one coordinated workstream

* Link data model / status values;
* Link manager create/edit/end-of-life UX;
* Deal Close and Deal Archive behavior;
* WAGR-456 payload eligibility and serialized status/state;
* WAGR-491 Exclude/Delete rules;
* CMS omission semantics / tombstone expectations;
* WAGR-459 staging tests;
* migration/backfill of existing inactive Links;
* reporting/history/SLC attribution.

## Questions for WagerTech / Strah

1. Is Archived terminal for a Link?
2. Should Deal Archive move all child Links to Archived rather than Inactive?
3. Should Deal Close archive Links, or only deactivate them?
4. Should Archived Links remain in future payloads?
5. If omitted, does CMS retain the last-known state?
6. Can an Archived Link ever be restored, or must a new Link be created?

## Done when

Decision is recorded in Confluence and the affected Jira stories are updated together. Do not implement Link Archived piecemeal before this review.

**DRAFT — for Kobi/Taryn review before grooming**

**Context**
Emily asked for a quick-action button on each Sign-Up table row to log a sign-up in a pop-up (WAGR-436). The standard list view cannot do this. Row dropdown actions are limited, and bulk actions cannot be used for Log Sign Up or Complete Sign Up because each record needs its own input.

Kobi (Slack, 2026-10-02): a custom LWC-based list view with row-level action buttons may be possible, but not for V1. V1 UX is built around the Split view. This is a post-go-live enhancement to scope and prioritize against the other post-go-live work the client wants.

**Requirements (proposed, to confirm)**

* Custom LWC list view for Sign-Ups with an **Action** column on each row.
* One primary action button per row (for example, Log Sign Up / Complete Sign Up, based on row status).
* A caret menu for secondary actions (for example, Open details).
* Row actions are defined by Jumpr. Edit, Delete, Change Owner and Edit Labels do not show to non-admin users.
* Reference pattern: the Redeposits prototype "My Redeposits" list view (primary button per row plus caret menu). Attach Kobi's screenshot of it.

**Open questions**

* Which actions and statuses need row-level buttons, and which fields appear in the pop-up vs. the full record? (Not specified by Emily.)
* Does the custom list view replace the standard list view or sit next to it?
* Size and priority vs. other post-go-live work. Do not estimate until scoped.
* Do the Split view and this list view need to work together?

**Constraints / Dependencies**

* Out of V1 scope. Depends on go-live.
* Related: WAGR-436 (V1 work: remove row dropdown actions for non-admins, confirm Log Sign Up / Complete Sign Up flows still work for non-admin users).
* Bulk actions (bulk archive, fraud flagging) are separate V2 stories, only if the client asks.

**Source**

* WAGR-436, Sep 29 update (per Kobi).
* Kobi Slack message, 2026-10-02, 10:46 AM ET: https://jumpr-solutions.slack.com/archives/C0BRW5L8SUA/p1790952381598149
* Wagertech Internal Sync, 2026-10-02 (ticket 436 discussion).
